content.text:
### Spec Compliance
- ✅ **Spec compliant.** Every file the brief names exists at HEAD: `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `index.html`, `src/main.ts`, `src/levels/index.ts`, `test/smoke/sanity.test.ts`, `README.md`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` (all new-file hunks in the diff, stat line 7–17 = 10 files). `package.json:9` is `tsc --noEmit && vite build`; `package.json:8/10/11/12/13` are `dev`/`preview`/`test`/`test:watch`/`smoke` exactly as specified.
- ✅ **Verbatim where the brief was literal:** `tsconfig.json:1-18`, `index.html:1-12` (incl. `lang="zh-CN"`:2, `#app`:9, module script:10), `src/main.ts:1-2`, `test/smoke/sanity.test.ts:1-8`, `src/levels/index.ts:1`, `README.md:1-8` all match brief Steps 2/4/5/7/9 character for character.
- ✅ **Zero runtime dependencies:** `package.json` has no `dependencies` key at all; `pnpm-lock.yaml:7-25` shows the sole importer carrying only `devDependencies`, and 0 React/zustand/immer/date libs appear anywhere in the lockfile. All five packages sit in `devDependencies` (`package.json:15-21`).
- ✅ **README affiliation/copyright requirement met:** `README.md:5` states no affiliation with LevelHead and not an official work; `README.md:7` states study/personal use only and no commercial distribution; `README.md:6,8` state no original art/audio/text/fonts, procedural graphics, original copy, and support-the-original. Requirement at `task-1-brief.md:146-149` is satisfied in full.
- ✅ **No copied material:** the whole diff is text; the stat summary lists no binary/asset/font/audio file, and the only non-original wording is the brief-supplied README paragraph.
- ✅ **Encoding:** byte-checked all nine committed text files for a UTF-8 BOM (checks run below) — `BOM=False` for all nine.
- ✅ **Commit format:** `a9b81d6 chore: scaffold vite + vitest project with sanity test` — English, `type: summary`.
- ✅ **Config can host every later test directory — verified, not assumed.** `vite.config.ts:12` `include: ['test/**/*.test.ts']` covers `test/core`, `test/levels`, `test/app`, `test/persist`, `test/ui`, `test/smoke`; `tsconfig.json:17` includes `src`/`test`. I checked what the later tests actually need a DOM for: plan `:4433` (`test/ui/view.test.ts` = pure camera/hit-test functions), plan `:5355-5360` (`test/ui/panels.test.ts`, the phase's only DOM test, declares `// @vitest-environment jsdom` as its first line), plan `:4177-4245` (`test/persist/storage.test.ts` is a pure serialize/migrate/round-trip test) and plan `:4272` (`globalThis.localStorage?.` optional chaining, so node is fine), plan `:4300+` (`test/app/commands.test.ts` pure logic). Playwright's `test/smoke/ui.spec.ts` (plan `:5522`) is **not** matched by `*.test.ts`, so Vitest and Playwright will not double-run it.
- ✅ **Deviation A (jsdom 28.1.0) is justified.** `https://registry.npmjs.org/jsdom/28.0.1` → HTTP 404 `version not found: 28.0.1`; `https://registry.npmjs.org/jsdom/28.1.0` → HTTP 200 with `integrity sha512-0+MoQNYyr2rBHqO1xilltfDjV9G7ymYGlAUazgcDLQaUf8JDHbuGwsxN6U9qWaElZ4w1B2r7yEGIL3GdeW3Rug==`, byte-identical to `pnpm-lock.yaml:326`. `package.json:17` is therefore the smallest correct substitution; jsdom is unused by any committed test today, so blast radius is nil.
- ✅ **Deviation B (`vite.config.ts:1`) is justified.** `node_modules/vitest/dist/config.d.ts:28-34` really does declare `module "vite" { interface UserConfig { test?: VitestInlineConfig } }`, and `tsconfig.json:15` `types: ["vitest/globals"]` suppresses automatic `@types` inclusion, so nothing loads that augmentation; without the reference `defineConfig` from `vite` has no `test` key and `pnpm build`'s `tsc --noEmit` fails. The line is a comment, stripped by the bundler. (`import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'` would be equivalent — no change needed.)
- ✅ **Deviation C (`environmentMatchGlobs` → per-file docblock) is justified and the replacement works.** Check: grep for `environmentMatchGlobs` across `node_modules/vitest` → **0 matches**, so it is absent from both runtime and the bundled `.d.ts` (which also means `InlineConfig` rejects it, matching the reported TS2769). The brief's key at `task-1-brief.md:79` was dead at runtime *and* fatal to `pnpm build` — the brief's own acceptance criterion. The replacement (`vite.config.ts:11-20`) grants node by default and jsdom per file, which still gives `test/ui/panels.test.ts` its DOM while letting the DOM-free `view.test.ts` run on node. A forgotten docblock fails loudly with `document is not defined`, not silently.
- ✅ **Extra file (Deviation D) is narrow and load-bearing:** `pnpm-workspace.yaml:1-5` exempts exactly the four pinned dev packages from the minimum-release-age gate that the report quotes blocking `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Its provenance is not host-npmrc-driven (checks below), which is consistent with a pnpm-11 toolchain default — i.e. it protects Tasks 2–12, not just this host. No runtime dependency is affected.
- ⚠️ **Cannot verify from diff — `pnpm dev`:** only the report's manual probe (`GET /` and `GET /src/main.ts` → 200, §2) evidences it; nothing in the diff does. The config is the standard `index.html` + `src/main.ts` + `dev: vite` triad, so the risk is low; the controller can confirm in seconds if it wants an artifact rather than a claim.
- ⚠️ **Cannot verify from diff — release-age policy provenance:** I found no source for it in `~/.npmrc` (only `registry=https://registry.npmmirror.com`), `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pnpm\config\rc`, `%APPDATA%\pnpm\config\rc`, `~/.pnpmfile.cjs`, or `npm_config_*`/`pnpm` env (only `PNPM_HOME`). `web_search` was unavailable (no `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`), so I could not confirm pnpm 11's documented default. Controller: if the gate is *not* a pnpm-11 default, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is an environment workaround rather than a required file — it should then be reconsidered.
- ⚠️ **Cannot verify from diff — install reproducibility:** I did not re-run `pnpm install` (read-only review; it would mutate `node_modules`/lockfile). The fresh-clone → install → test → build result is the report's claim (§2), supported by a self-consistent committed lockfile.

**Checks run (named risk → what I checked):** jsdom pin existence → npm registry 404/200 pair above; `test` key typecheck → `node_modules/vitest/dist/config.d.ts:28-34` + `tsconfig.json:15`; `environmentMatchGlobs` removal → grep of `node_modules/vitest` (0 matches); later-test accommodation → plan greps for `@vitest-environment`/`test/ui/` and planned test paths + read of plan `:4170-4319`; release-age provenance → host config/env scan; encoding → BOM byte check on all 9 files; repo hygiene → root `.gitignore` (unchanged at base, so absent from the diff) covers `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `coverage/`, `playwright-report/`, `test-results/`.

### Strengths
- The implementer's four conflict write-ups are accurate in every checkable particular: the jsdom version really is a 404, the module augmentation really is at `config.d.ts:28-34`, and `environmentMatchGlobs` really is gone from Vitest 5. I found no inflated or fabricated evidence.

content.text:
### Spec Compliance

- ✅ **Runtime dependencies exactly 0** — the change adds only two new files; no `package.json`/lockfile hunk exists in [review-04ceeaf..fd82f2b.diff](.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase0/review-04ceeaf..fd82f2b.diff#L6-L9). Nothing to install, nothing added.
- ✅ **Signals are 0/1, one bit per slot, low bit first** — [signal.ts:68-73](src/core/signal.ts#L68-L73), [signal.ts:76-86](src/core/signal.ts#L76-L86). Verified at slot granularity, not just by round-trip: [signal.test.ts:34-43](test/core/signal.test.ts#L34-L43) asserts `getBit(base)`, `base+1`, `base+2`, `base+7` individually for `0b1010_0101`.
- ✅ **`width > 8` → `Uint8Array`, low byte first** — [signal.ts:93-97](src/core/signal.ts#L93-L97) packs `bytes[i >> 3] |= 1 << (i & 7)`, so byte 0 carries bits 0–7; [signal.test.ts:45-50](test/core/signal.test.ts#L45-L50) round-trips `[0x34, 0x12]`. `width <= 8` returns a `number` ([signal.ts:88-92](src/core/signal.ts#L88-L92)), matching the brief's Step 1 tests exactly.
- ✅ **Fixed capacity 65536, never reallocates, no growth path** — one `Uint8Array` allocated at [signal.ts:49](src/core/signal.ts#L49), never reassigned; the only mutation of `size` is the bump at [signal.ts:63](src/core/signal.ts#L63). No `growTo` exists (check: `grep growTo|grow` over `src/` returns only the doc comment). Identity is pinned by [signal.test.ts:83-92](test/core/signal.test.ts#L83-L92).
- ✅ **`alloc` throws `RangeError` naming the capacity** — [signal.ts:61](src/core/signal.ts#L61) `signal table is full: need N slots, capacity is ${capacity}`; exercised at the boundary (`size === capacity`, `alloc(1)`) by [signal.test.ts:77-81](test/core/signal.test.ts#L77-L81).
- ✅ **`Port` reads and writes through the table (live view)** — [signal.ts:121-122](src/core/signal.ts#L121-L122) closes over `table`/`base` with no cached value; [signal.test.ts:96-103](test/core/signal.test.ts#L96-L103) asserts port→table visibility via `t.getPort(p.base, 3)`.
- ✅ **Commit format** — `feat(core): add bit-level signal table and ports`, English `type: summary` ([diff:4](.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase0/review-04ceeaf..fd82f2b.diff#L4)).
- ✅ **Claim 1 verified — the brief does contradict itself, and the implementer resolved it on the correct side.** Brief Step 3 (`n.toString(2).padStart(width, '0')`) yields `'101'` for `formatPort(0b101, 1, 2)` because `padStart` never truncates, so it cannot satisfy brief:110. The test is not the wrong expectation: its title is "pads binary to the port width", and choosing an over-wide value (`0b101`) for a 1-bit port is only meaningful if binary output is defined as exactly `width` characters — which is also what the port can physically hold. Step 4's acceptance ("12 passed") is unreachable otherwise. Masking at [signal.ts:153](src/core/signal.ts#L153) is the right repair, and it was disclosed as a deviation ([task-2-report.md:244-248](.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase0/task-2-report.md#L244-L248)) rather than hidden by editing the test.
- ✅ **Claim 2 verified — the brief's "15 passed" is arithmetically wrong and the 15th test is legitimate, not padding.** Step 1 has 12 `it` blocks (7 + 2 + 2 + 1); Step 5 adds 2 → 14. The added [signal.test.ts:83-92](test/core/signal.test.ts#L83-L92) is the only test that pins the load-bearing invariant the global constraints name explicitly ("`slots` must remain the same `Uint8Array` instance for the table's lifetime"); the other two Step 5 tests cover value survival and the capacity throw, neither of which asserts identity. Not padding.
- ✅ **Claim 3 verified unreachable in Phase 0 — and the reasoning holds for exactly the right reason.** Both flagged defects require `width > 8`, and every pin declared anywhere in the plan is `width: 1` (check: `grep 'width: *[0-9]+'` over the plan → 48 hits, all 1; the only 4-bit output was replaced by four 1-bit outputs, [progress.md:73](.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase0/progress.md#L73)). The current tree has no consumer of `signal.ts` at all (check: `grep` for `createSignalTable|createPort|formatPort|valuesEqual` over `src/` → only `src/core/signal.ts` itself).
- ✅ **Claim 4 verified — the `growTo` note is stale and omitting it is correct.** Brief:291 refers to a function its own Step 3 does not contain; the plan itself had already ruled the growth draft a real defect and replaced it with fixed capacity + explicit `RangeError` (check: plan:5961, and the plan's Step 3 block at plan:461-513 contains no `growTo`). The implementer matched the plan's ruling, not merely the reviewer's constraint.
- ⚠️ **Cannot verify from the diff:** the report's raw `pnpm test` (12→15, 16/16) and `pnpm build` transcripts. Nothing in the requirement set depends on them, and the test count is independently checkable from the diff: counting the `it(` blocks gives 10 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 15, and reconstructing the file from the brief's Step 1 (104 content lines + 27 inserted lines) yields exactly the diff's 131 lines.
- Check I ran (no suite re-run): node one-liner `new Uint8Array(1.5).length` → `1` (no throw), and a 12-bit set/get round trip → `[0x34]`; the implementer's edge-case (a) description is accurate.

### Strengths

- The fixed-capacity contract is honored in the strongest form available: the array is allocated once ([signal.ts:49](src/core/signal.ts#L49)), `size` is a getter over a closure variable ([signal.ts:50-52](src/core/signal.ts#L50-L52)), and internal methods read through `table.slots` rather than a captured copy ([signal.ts:68-101](src/core/signal.ts#L68-L101)) — so the two ways this invariant is normally lost (reassignment, cached reference) are both closed, and one of them is now tested.
- The capacity guard is placed before `base` is handed out ([signal.ts:59-64](src/core/signal.ts#L59-L64)), so a failed `alloc` cannot leak a partially-committed base or mutate `size`.
- `formatPort`'s fix uses `% 2 ** width` rather than `& ((1 << width) - 1)`, which is correct for values beyond the 32-bit boundary; the reason is recorded at [signal.ts:149-152](src/core/signal.ts#L149-L152) rather than left implicit.
- The test file is the brief's Step 1 content verbatim — the implementer fixed the implementation to fit the test, not the reverse, and disclosed the one-line deviation and the count discrepancy instead of quietly normalizing both.

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)

- None.

#### Important (Should Fix)

- **[signal.ts:93](src/core/signal.ts#L93) vs [signal.ts:31](src/core/signal.ts#L31) — plan-mandated: `getPort` sizes its buffer with `width / 8` (floored) while `assertWidth` requires `Math.ceil(width / 8)` bytes.** `assertWidth` (an exported function) accepts `setPort(base, 12, Uint8Array([0x34, 0x12]))`, and `getPort(base, 12)` then returns one byte — bits 8–11 are silently discarded. So the module's own public contract admits input that its own reader corrupts. Verified by running the exact pair: read-back is `[0x34]`. Reachability is genuinely nil in Phase 0 (no pin exceeds width 1), which is why the implementer's deferral is defensible — but for Task 5 the symptom is not a wrong value, it is a *misdiagnosis*: `Simulation.settle` compares `prev = getPort(base, width)` against the def's output via `portsEqual`, a 1-byte vs 2-byte mismatch makes `changed` permanently true, and the circuit reports `UnstableCircuitError` after 512 iterations. Fix is one word and test-neutral: `new Uint8Array(Math.ceil(width / 8))` at [signal.ts:93](src/core/signal.ts#L93) (all existing tests use width 16, so nothing else moves). If the controller prefers to keep the brief's code byte-for-byte, record the accepted risk explicitly for Tasks 5 and 6 rather than leaving it as a report footnote.

#### Minor (Nice to Have)

content.text:
## Finding Verdicts

- **Finding 1:** **ADDRESSED** — `src/core/signal.ts:33`: `const bytes = new Uint8Array(Math.ceil(width / 8));` replaces the floored `width / 8` (only the `width > 8` branch is affected; `width <= 8` returns the `number` branch untouched, and multiples of 8 are arithmetically unchanged, so the width-16 contract is preserved). The amended line is genuinely covered: the new test `reads back every bit of a wide port whose width is not a multiple of 8` (diff lines 59–68) uses width 12, where `ceil` (2) ≠ `floor` (1), and the report's RED run shows it failing pre-fix with `expected Uint8Array[ 52 ] to deeply equal Uint8Array[ 52, 2 ]` — that assertion is only satisfiable by the ceil sizing. Expected `[0x34, 0x02]` is arithmetically correct: slot 9 is the only set bit above 7 after `setPort` writes 12 slots from `[0x34, 0x12]`, so the high byte is `0b10`.
- **Finding 2:** **ADDRESSED** — `test/core/signal.test.ts` (diff lines 91–114): the test now fills to capacity (`createSignalTable(8)` → `alloc(8)`), attempts one more allocation inside `try { t.alloc(1) } catch (err) { refusal = err }`, then asserts `expect(refusal).toBeInstanceOf(RangeError)`, `expect(t.slots).toBe(slots)`, `expect(t.getPort(base, 8)).toBe(0b1111_0000)` and the two raw `slots[...]` values. This is a real sharpening, not a cosmetic one — see next section for the mutant judgment. Provenance is clean: this test is *not* one of the brief's Step 1 tests (brief lines 31–126 list the 12 Step 1 `it` blocks; `never swaps its backing slots` is the implementer-added 15th test per report §5 Conflict 2), and the diff's single removed line (`- expect(t.slots).toBe(slots);`) sits inside that self-added test, so no Step 1 assertion was edited.

**Probe-file and mutant claims (judged, not accepted):**

- *No probe file survives.* Confirmed from the diff stat header: exactly `src/core/signal.ts` and `test/core/signal.test.ts`, +36/−2, one commit, and no hunk anywhere for `test/core/__probe.test.ts` or any other scratch path.
- *The reshaped assertion would fail against a grow-on-demand implementation: yes, decisively.* A table that grows only when full-and-asked-for-more cannot throw on `t.alloc(1)` at `size === capacity === 8` — it grows and returns a base, so `refusal` stays `undefined` and `expect(undefined).toBeInstanceOf(RangeError)` fails on its own. The identity assertion is a second, independent net: a `Uint8Array` cannot grow in place, so any growth relocates the backing array and `expect(t.slots).toBe(slots)` fails (as would `getPort(base, 8)` and the raw-slot reads, which read the stale captured reference). The report's mutant output is consistent with this (`net 1: expected undefined to be an instance of RangeError`; `net 2: relocated backing array`). I verified this by reading the test's control flow rather than by re-running a mutant — writing a probe into the tree under review was not appropriate for a scoped re-review, so this leg rests on static reasoning plus the report's recorded mutant run.

## New Breakage in the Fix Diff

**None.**

- The change is one line in a branch that no pre-existing test enters with a non-multiple-of-8 width; the only pre-existing wide-port test (width 16) is byte-identical in behaviour (`ceil(16/8) === 16/8 === 2`).
- The only observable shape change is intended and self-consistent: for widths 9–15 etc., `getPort`/`Port.read()` now returns the same `ceil(width/8)`-byte length that `assertWidth`/`setPort` already accepted, instead of a truncated one. No in-tree consumer exists yet (`net.ts`, level checker not built), and nothing in the diff depends on the old length.
- Constraint check on the diff itself: `formatPort` is absent from the diff (untouched); `package.json`/lockfile/config files are absent from the diff; commit message is `fix(core): size wide port read-back buffer with ceil(width / 8)`, matching `type: summary`.
- Evidence legibility: the report's RED/GREEN/full/build blocks are present, with exact commands, exit codes, and counts that are mutually consistent (11 `SignalTable` + 2 `Port` + 2 `formatPort` + 1 `valuesEqual` = 16 focused; 16 + 1 sanity = 17 full; +36/−2 matches the diff stat). Nothing in the diff raised a doubt that needed an independent run.

## Out-of-Scope Observations

Deferred items for the controller's ledger; none extend this loop:

1. **`valuesEqual` cannot equate the two representations of one wide value** — `valuesEqual(0x1234, new Uint8Array([0x34, 0x12])) === false` because `numberToBytes` always emits 4 bytes (report §6 item 3). This is a live data-shape trap for the level checker: an expected value written as a number will never match a 16-bit port read back as `Uint8Array`. Needs normalization on the checker side or a width parameter.
2. **`alloc` accepts non-integer and negative widths** (`alloc(1.5)` → base 0, `size` 1.5; `alloc(-2)` throws `/positive/`), and `assertWidth` is asymmetric on negatives (`assertWidth(-1, 32)` no throw vs `<-1, 31>` throws) — report §6 item 5.
3. **No bounds checking on `setBit`/`getBit`** — out-of-range writes are silently dropped and reads return 0 (report §6 item 4); deliberate for the hot path, recorded so it is not re-litigated.
4. **Round-trip is still lossy above `width` inside the top byte** (`getPort(base, 12)` after `setPort(..., [0x34, 0x12])` → `[0x34, 0x02]`). Inherent to a `width`-bit port and now explicitly asserted, but any caller expecting `valuesEqual(input, output)` on a non-multiple-of-8 port will be surprised.
5. **Report hygiene:** the §5 probe table row at `task-2-report.md:220` still records the pre-fix behaviour (`getPort(base,12)` returns `Uint8Array([0x34])`), which now contradicts the fixed code. The report self-declares this stale row as an intentionally unedited Minor; it is documentation-only and does not affect the shipped artefact.
6. **Forward-referencing source comment:** the new comment in `getPort` cites a downstream misdiagnosis via `Simulation.settle`/`net.ts`, neither of which exists in this tree yet. Explanatory only, no behavioural claim.

## Verdict

**All findings addressed.** Finding 1 is fixed at the amended line and covered by a discriminating width-12 regression test that demonstrably failed pre-fix; Finding 2's reshaped assertion now has two independent nets against the exact grow-on-demand mutant the old shape was blind to. The fix diff introduces no new Critical or Important breakage, respects all stated constraints (fixed-capacity design intact, `formatPort` untouched, Step 1 tests unedited, no dependency change, commit format correct), and leaves no probe artefact behind.

Task 2 is complete, so I'm updating the ledger with the findings and moving forward. Instead of creating shared tasks for each remaining item, I'll track everything in the ledger and my todo list to conserve context. The out-of-scope observations go into the ledger as deferred items, then I'll dispatch Task 3 with a head commit of ec166d8.

**Status:** DONE_WITH_CONCERNS

**Commit:** `2fc391c` feat(core): add component registry, base defs and bit fields

**Tests:** full suite 41/41 pass (registry 24, incl. the brief's 18 verbatim) + `pnpm build` (tsc --noEmit && vite build) green; zero dependency changes.

**Concerns (need Lead confirmation):**
1. The brief's Step 5 snippet cannot pass the brief's own Step 1 tests. Two forced changes: (a) constant sources are `category: 'io'`, since the test asserts `byCategory('logic1')` excludes `const_on`; (b) `delay_line.evaluate` mirrors its input and `mem1.clockEdge` mirrors the new state into the output array — an empty `evaluate` cannot yield the values asserted at test lines 128/141 because `evaluate` gets no `state`. Both paths are dead code in the kernel (Task 5's `settle()` skips sequential defs; `tick()` discards the `out` array it passes to `clockEdge`), so simulation semantics are unchanged; documented in code comments and §1.3 of the report. Alternative is relaxing those two test assertions.
2. Brief bookkeeping is stale: Step 6 expects "14 passed", actual 18 (24 with my 6 additive tests).
3. `fields.ts` is 32-bit only (`1 << i` wraps at 32) — fine for Phase 0, noted for Phase 1 wide values.

**Report:** `D:\Documents\turing-complete\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase0\task-3-report.md`

I'm seeing two key test failures. The first is that constant sources need to be categorized as 'io' rather than 'logic1' based on the test expectations, and the second involves the delay_line.evaluate and mem1.clockEdge implementations, which I need to clarify — there's something about how these components mirror their inputs that's causing issues.

Looking at the design, the original brief had delay_line's evaluate as a no-op with a comment explaining that the kernel publishes the held value before settle() runs. But the implementer is saying that an empty evaluate can't produce the values the tests expect because the test harness calls evaluate directly with undefined state. I need to check the actual test code and the decide module to understand what's really happening here. The core issue is that my Task 5 kernel design has settle() skipping sequential defs entirely, but then tick() snapshots inputs, calls clockEdge, and publishes state afterward — so the logic should work, but there's a mismatch in how the test is structured versus how the kernel actually behaves. So the tests in Task 3 directly evaluate delay_line, but since it's marked sequential and has no evaluate method, it gets skipped entirely—which should fail those assertions unless the implementation explicitly added an evaluate function. This creates a critical conflict: if delay_line has both an evaluate and a clockEdge, then Task 5's settle() will invoke the evaluate every iteration, which means it needs to read the held state and mirror the output correctly to avoid instability.

The solution is to keep evaluate on sequential components but have it republish the held state rather than reading the input—that way settle() becomes a no-op semantically but stays consistent with the kernel's design. The clockEdge should only mutate the state array, with the kernel handling publication afterward. This approach resolves the conflict between Task 3's tests and Task 5's implementation strategy.

However, there's a subtlety with mem1: since its state is written by clockEdge and read back by evaluate, I need to be careful about how the publish logic works when state updates within the same tick. The real fix is to let Task 5's kernel own the state publication, while Task 3's tests should verify clockEdge behavior and state directly rather than testing evaluate in isolation. I could add an evaluate function that mirrors state back to outputs, or I could restructure the tests to avoid calling evaluate on sequential components altogether, but that feels like sidestepping the actual issue. The cleaner approach is to make evaluate publish the state it holds, keeping the kernel contract intact. I need to actually read the test code and implementation file to make an informed ruling on whether the sibling task's test is wrong. This is a conflict between Task 3's tests and Task 5's design that I need to adjudicate.

{"file_path": "D:\Documents\turing-complete\docs\superpowers\plans\2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase0.md", "new_string": "> **`evaluate` 必须接收 `state`**（对初稿的修正，Task 3 实测发现的真实缺陷）。存储元件的输出只能来自它保存的值；若 `evaluate` 拿不到 `state`，它就只能去读当前输入——那样「延迟线」会退化成一根直通的缓冲器。实测证据：`clockEdge` 把 1 存进 state 后，再调 `evaluate([0], …)`，输出立刻变成 0，而真正的延迟线此刻必须仍然输出 1。
>
> 因此约定是：**`evaluate` 对存储元件 = 把保持的值发布到输出**；`clockEdge` **只改 state，不写输出**。
>

- **Storage semantics finding: ADDRESSED**

  - `evaluate` now publishes from `state` and never reads inputs: [defs/index.ts](src/core/defs/index.ts#L135-L141) (`delay_line`) and [defs/index.ts](src/core/defs/index.ts#L159-L165) (`mem1`) — `o[0] = state?.[0] === 1 ? 1 : 0`.
  - `clockEdge` samples state only and writes no outputs: [defs/index.ts](src/core/defs/index.ts#L140-L142), [defs/index.ts](src/core/defs/index.ts#L163-L165); the old `mem1` `o[0] = state[0] === 1 ? 1 : 0` mirror is gone (diff line 304-310).
  - Signature: `state` third, before `ctx` — [registry.ts](src/core/registry.ts#L45-L54); the false "never reached through the kernel" comment is deleted and replaced by a contract comment ([defs/index.ts](src/core/defs/index.ts#L119-L126) region, diff lines 245-255).
  - Tests are genuinely discriminating: `evaluate` is called with the **opposite polarity** to the held value at [registry.test.ts](test/core/registry.test.ts#L139) (held 1, input 0) and [registry.test.ts](test/core/registry.test.ts#L144) (held 0, input 1), and `clockEdge`-must-not-write-outputs at [registry.test.ts](test/core/registry.test.ts#L157).
  - RED evidence is real, not merely asserted. The quoted failures (`test/core/registry.test.ts:134:20` "expected +0 to be 1", `:151:20` "expected 1 to be +0") are exactly the two discriminating assertions, offset by −6 from the shipped lines 140/157, i.e. captured with the rewritten tests before the 6-line header comment was added. Against the shipped `2fc391c` bodies this is arithmetically forced: old `delay_line.evaluate` = `o[0] = i[0]===1?1:0` yields 0 for `[0]`, and old `mem1.clockEdge` mirrors state into `o[0]` = 1 where 0 is required. The report's 9 TS2554 line numbers (75, 84, 86, 88, 90, 104, 107, 115, 165) likewise equal the shipped call sites minus the same 6-line offset — the evidence is internally consistent.
  - Task 5 plan amendment matches the ruling: [plan](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase0.md#L1889-L1894) iterates every def with an `evaluate`, passes `this.#state[index]` third, reuses one `out` array, no `sequential` special-case; the new `a delay line holds its sampled value when its input changes` test is present at [plan](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase0.md#L2095-L2122) and I traced it against the amended kernel — it passes only with state-publishing defs. `src/core/net.ts` does not exist yet, so no shipped kernel retains the old skip.
  - Scope guards hold: `fields.ts`, `signal.ts`/`formatPort`, `package.json`, every gate def untouched; commit `75f214e fix(core): …` is English `type: summary`.

- **Ruling's optional-parameter premise: IMPLEMENTER CORRECT** (one overstatement, caveat below)

  |---|---|

{"file_path": "D:\Documents\turing-complete\docs\superpowers\plans\2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase0.md", "new_string": "> **`evaluate` 必须接收 `state`**（对初稿的修正，Task 3 实测发现的真实缺陷）。存储元件的输出只能来自它保存的值；若 `evaluate` 拿不到 `state`，它就只能去读当前输入——那样「延迟线」会退化成一根直通的缓冲器。实测证据：`clockEdge` 把 1 存进 state 后，再调 `evaluate([0], …)`，输出立刻变成 0，而真正的延迟线此刻必须仍然输出 1。
>
> 因此约定是：**`evaluate` 对存储元件 = 把保持的值发布到输出**；`clockEdge` **只改 state，不写输出**。

>
> ```ts
> def.evaluate!([a, b], out, undefined, undefined, { tick: 0 });
> def.evaluate!([1], out, state, undefined, { tick: 0 });   // 存储元件才传真的 state
> ```
>
> 组合元件的**定义**不受影响，仍可写成 `evaluate: (i, o) => …`（TS 允许实参少于形参）。

{"description": "Implement Task 4: graph model", "prompt": "You are implementing Task 4: 电路文档模型 (`src/core/graph.ts`).

## Task Description

Read your task brief first: `D:\Documents\turing-complete\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase0\task-4-brief.md`
It is your requirements, with the exact values to use verbatim. Follow its steps in order.

## Context

We are building a from-scratch replica of the puzzle game *Turing Complete*: players wire logic gates out of NAND gates and work up to a CPU. This is Phase 0, a vertical slice covering chapter 1 (12 levels).

Done and green (full suite 41/41, `pnpm build` clean):
- Task 1 — project skeleton (Vite 8 + Vitest 5 + TS 5.9).
- Task 2 — `src/core/signal.ts`: fixed-capacity bit-level signal table, `PortValue`.
- Task 3 — `src/core/registry.ts` + `src/core/defs/index.ts` + `src/core/fields.ts`: the component catalog. 15 defs: `const_on`, `const_off`, `nand`, `not`, `and`, `or`, `nor`, `xor`, `xnor`, `and3`, `or3`, `delay_line`, `mem1`, `level_input`, `level_output`.

This task is the **editable document model** — the thing the canvas editor mutates and the thing that gets serialized to disk. Task 5 compiles a `Graph` into a runnable netlist; the UI (Task 11) mutates it through commands.

Work from: `D:\Documents\turing-complete` (git repo, branch `master`).

## Interfaces from earlier tasks you must use

- `registry.get(id)` **throws** `Error("unknown component: <id>")` for an unknown id. It does not return undefined. So anywhere the graph might reference an unknown def, guard with `registry.has(id)` first — `validateGraph` must not throw on a graph containing a bogus def, it must report it. The brief's tests cover exactly this.
- `ComponentDef` has `inputs` and `outputs` arrays of `PinDef` (`{ id, width, label? }`), plus `id`, `name: { zh, en }`, `category`, `cost`, `sequential`, `stateBytes`, and optionally `hidden`.
- `const_on` / `const_off` are `category: 'io'` with **no** inputs and one output. `level_input` has no inputs, one output. `level_output` has one input and one mirrored output. `delay_line` has one input, one output.

## Design decisions already made (do not re-litigate)

- Instance ids are `i1`, `i2`, … and wire ids are `w1`, `w2`, …; `nextId` scans existing ids for the highest numeric suffix and returns the next one. The brief's test pins `nextId('i', [{id:'i1'},{id:'i3'}]) === 'i4'` and `nextId('i', []) === 'i1'`.
- `validateGraph` returns **issues**, never throws. `severity: 'error'` is reserved for things that make the circuit meaningless (unknown def, wire pointing at a missing instance, wire pointing at a missing port, two wires driving one input). `severity: 'warning'` covers things the player may still be working on (an unwired input, a feedback loop).
- **A feedback loop is a warning, not an error.** Storage elements make legitimate loops, and the player is often mid-edit. The point where a combinational loop becomes fatal is the simulator (Task 5), which raises `UnstableCircuitError` when the circuit fails to settle. Do not turn it into an error here.
- The feedback-loop detection must be an **iterative** traversal, not recursive — a large circuit must not blow the JS stack. The brief's implementation uses an explicit grey/black colouring stack.
- `cloneGraph` must deep-copy instances, wires, and nested `customComponents` bodies, so editor undo can hold a snapshot without aliasing the live graph.

- `registry.get(id)` **throws** for an unknown id; guard with `registry.has(id)`.
- `ComponentDef.evaluate` signature is `(inputs, outputs, state, ctx)` where **`state` is a required third parameter** typed `Uint8Array | undefined`. This is load-bearing and was the subject of a real bug fix in Task 3 — see below.
- `ComponentDef.clockEdge` signature is `(inputs, outputs, state, ctx)` with `state: Uint8Array` (not optional).
- `createSignalTable(capacity)` — **pass an explicit capacity** sized for the circuit rather than relying on the 65536 default. Task 2's ledger note: 20,000 two-input gates at 3 slots each is 60,000 slots and any 3-input gate overruns the default. Derive a capacity from the compiled instance count (with headroom) and pass it.

## The storage-element contract (already fixed and shipped in Task 3 — build on it)

- **`evaluate` publishes the value the component is holding**, reading its `state` and never its inputs. `delay_line`'s body is `o[0] = state?.[0] === 1 ? 1 : 0`.
- **`clockEdge` samples inputs into `state` only** and must not write outputs.
- The kernel publishes state during `reset()` and `tick()`; `settle()` goes through the generic `evaluate` path.
- **`settle()` must NOT skip sequential defs.** It iterates every def that has an `evaluate`, passing `this.#state[index]` as the third argument. - **`delayOf` must be a linear-time DAG longest path** (Kahn topological order + one relaxation pass), not a path-enumerating DFS. A path walk is exponential on diamond-shaped circuits, which is exactly what CPU circuits are full of. The brief shows the correct implementation.

- `compile()` must resolve every input pin's driver slot up front: an unwired input reads from a dedicated zero slot. This keeps the settle loop branch-free.
- `Simulation.read(base, width)` / `write(base, width, value)` address **slots**, not names. Name-to-slot resolution lives on the `Netlist` (`net.inputBase("i3.a")`, `net.outputBase("i3.out")`), so level binding and grading each resolve a name once instead of per evaluation.

But then I realize the parallel Jacobi sweep is actually the right solution here. By computing all next values from the previous iteration's values simultaneously and only committing the changes afterward, I can detect oscillation deterministically - the ring alternates between two states and never reaches a fixed point, so we hit the iteration limit and throw the error.

The standard SR latch setup uses cross-coupled NANDs with the set and reset lines held low at rest, which maintains a stable state as long as exactly one of those inputs gets pulsed at a time. So the brief's cross-coupled NAND fixtures weren't actually unstable — they were stable. To create a real combinational loop for the unstable test, I need to use a two-inverter ring or cross-coupled NANDs with both free inputs tied high. This means Task 6's fixtures need fixing too. I also see the zero slot issue: sharing one slot for all unwired inputs breaks the slot count assertion and direct input writes. The solution the implementer used is better — each unwired input gets its own zero slot, so `inputBase` returns that slot and can be written directly. ### Spec Compliance

- ✅ `SETTLE_LIMIT = 512` exactly, and a loop that never settles raises a catchable, well-typed `UnstableCircuitError` carrying `iterations`/`blame` (`src/core/net.ts:7`, `src/core/net.ts:352`, `src/core/errors.ts:11-23`) — never a hang; asserted with `iterations === SETTLE_LIMIT` at `test/core/net.test.ts:127-130`.
- ✅ `compile()` rejects error-severity issues and accepts warnings (`src/core/net.ts:109-112`); verified severities: `unknown-def`/`unknown-instance`/`unknown-port`/`multiple-drivers` are `'error'`, `feedback-loop`/`dangling-input` are `'warning'` (`src/core/graph.ts:180-181,197-198,210-211,223-224,246-247,302-303,317-318`). A loop graph compiles and is then caught by `settle()` — the plan's Task 6 path (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase0.md:2627-2635`).
- ✅ Storage contract honored in `settle()`: sequential defs are **not** skipped — only defs with no `evaluate` are (`src/core/net.ts:326-331`), and they receive `this.#state[i]` third, combinational defs `undefined`; matches the required 4-arg signature (`src/core/registry.ts:45-50`).
- ✅ `settle()` no longer zeroes `level_input`: `level_input.evaluate` writes nothing (`src/core/defs/index.ts:101-103`), the sweep skips unstaged pins (`src/core/net.ts:335`, `src/core/net.ts:343`), so an externally written output slot survives a settle — pinned by `test/core/net.test.ts:176-188`. Claim verified.
- ✅ Bit-by-bit change detection is necessary, not cosmetic: `valuesEqual(0xabc, <2-byte read-back>)` is `false` because `numberToBytes` always produces 4 bytes (`src/core/signal.ts:131-147`) while `getPort` returns `Uint8Array` for width > 8 (`src/core/signal.ts:87-103`); the brief's local `portsEqual` had the same length mismatch. Claim verified; discriminated by `test/core/net.test.ts:240-265`.
- ✅ `drive` is per-bit and starts at the identity (`src/core/net.ts:155-156`), wire width is `min(from,to)` (`src/core/net.ts:166`), so "an unwired input reads 0" holds from the zeroed table (`src/core/signal.ts:104-106`) and each unwired pin is independently writable — pinned by `test/core/net.test.ts:96-104`. This also keeps `slotCount` equal to pin bits (`test/core/net.test.ts:26-32`), which the brief's extra `zeroSlot` broke.
- ✅ `tick()` snapshots pre-edge inputs before applying any edge: sample loop copies inputs into `pending` (`src/core/net.ts:368-374`), all `clockEdge` calls run afterwards (`src/core/net.ts:377-381`), and `#publishState()` runs only after every edge (`src/core/net.ts:382`) — state changes are invisible within one tick, and a `clockEdge`'s writes to `outputs` are discarded, enforcing "must not write outputs" (`src/core/registry.ts:51-61`).
- ✅ `reset()` clears the table, clears state, resets the counter, publishes, re-settles (`src/core/net.ts:237-243`); the test's post-`tick` reset would fail if state were not cleared (`test/core/net.test.ts:267-280`).
- ✅ `delayOf` is linear-time Kahn + one relaxation (`src/core/net.ts:407-460`, no path enumeration) and breaks the path in **both** directions: the edge filter drops any wire touching a sequential node (`src/core/net.ts:432`) and storage sources are worth 0 (`src/core/net.ts:445`). Cross-validated against the plan's own expected metric for `andSolution()`: `delay: 2` (`plan:2966`) is exactly what this code returns for level_input(0) → nand(1) → not(1) → level_output(0).
- ✅ Gate delay convention matches the global constraint: `cost` is 1 for gates and 0 for sources/plumbing/storage (`src/core/defs/index.ts:22-25,44-47,85-89,92-120,126-166`), so "1 gate per component, storage contributes 0" is what `delayOf` sums.
- ✅ `read`/`write` address slots, name→slot resolution stays on the Netlist (`src/core/net.ts:183-184`, `src/core/net.ts:392-398`).
- ✅ Zero runtime dependencies: the commit adds only `src/core/errors.ts`, `src/core/net.ts`, `test/core/net.test.ts` (diff stat, lines 6-10); `package.json` untouched. Commit subject is English `type: summary` (diff line 4).
- ✅ No stale "unreachable" framing survives: grep for `TODO|FIXME|unreachable|cannot happen|XXX|HACK` over `src/core/net.ts` returns nothing, and `delayOf`'s comment now correctly says the loop is a *warning* rather than claiming `validateGraph` already rejected it (`src/core/net.ts:455-460`).
- Extra (benign): `expandedCount` duplicates `instanceCount` (`src/core/net.ts:26-27,178-179`), and `instanceIds()`/`outputKeys()`/`Simulation.registry` (`src/core/net.ts:185,187,208`) are unused by Tasks 6-7. The brief's own header and its Step 4 code name different shapes, so shipping the union is a deliberate hedge — but it is surface that will drift.
- ⚠️ Cannot verify from diff (empirically): the claim "a long combinational chain converges" and the exact `depth ≤ 511` boundary are analytic — one gate level propagates per sweep (`src/core/net.ts:324-350`), so a chain of depth *d* settles in *d+1* sweeps and depth ≥ 512 raises. The deepest test chain is 2 gates (`test/core/net.test.ts:82-94`), and I ran no tests (read-only checkout). Controller should add a 64-gate chain test (expect `stable === true`, `iterations === 65`) and a 512-gate test (expect the throw) to pin it.
- ⚠️ Cannot verify from diff: "safe for Task 6" is verified against the plan's `bindLevelIo`/`runRow` source (`plan:2450-2497,2607-2615,2642-2655`), not against Task 6's shipped code, which does not exist yet. Controller should re-check when Task 6 lands that writes still go through `outputBase('IN_x.out')`.
- ⚠️ Cannot verify from diff: the report's 7/16 RED table (brief-literal transcription) is not reproducible without writing files into the checkout. I reproduced its three decisive root causes analytically instead: shared `zeroSlot` (`plan:1799-1801`), in-place ring finding a fixed point (`plan:1900-1925`), and `out[p] ?? 0` destroying `level_input` (`plan:1917`).

Checks I ran outside the diff (one per named risk): `src/core/signal.ts:4-13,21-37,48-107,131-147` (does `#holds`' direct `slots` access and `capacityFor`'s capacity argument rest on real API? yes — `slots` is public per-slot 0/1, LSB-first, `createSignalTable(capacity)` exists); `src/core/registry.ts:22-66` + `tsconfig.json:17` (does the test's custom `ComponentDef` typecheck under `pnpm build`? yes — `'wide'` is in `ComponentCategory`, and `test` is in tsc's program); `src/core/defs/index.ts:85-166` (are `cost`/`evaluate`/`clockEdge` as claimed? yes); `src/core/graph.ts:180-318` (severity split for `compile`'s filter? yes); `plan:2262-2281,2450-2497,2553-2635,2642-2655,2966,2979-2995` (does Task 6/7 rely on the deviations? yes, both); grep for `width: [2-9]|[1-9][0-9]` across `src/` and the plan (are any multi-bit pins reachable in Phase 0? no, none).

### Deviation Adjudications

- **Settle algorithm: correct fix.** I traced the shipped sweep (stage all outputs from the previously committed table, then commit — `src/core/net.ts:318-350`) and the brief's in-place sweep by hand on the Lead's corrected fixture: in-place returns `stable` at iteration 2 with the self-consistent pair (n1=1, n2=0), because `(1,0)` and `(0,1)` are genuine fixed points of a two-inverter ring; the Jacobi orbit from the zero-initialised table is `(0,0)→(1,1)→(0,0)` and never converges, so it throws. The plan's own corrected Task 6/7 fixtures expect exactly that throw (`plan:2262-2281`, `plan:2979-2995`), so **the brief's algorithm cannot satisfy the plan's downstream assertions and the deviation is required, not preferred**. It is also order-independent and *sound*: `settle()` returns `stable` only when every staged output already equals the table (`src/core/net.ts:341-350`), so a period-2 orbit can never be reported as stable. On long chains it converges in `depth+1` sweeps — a 100-gate ripple settles in 101, not 1 — so `SETTLE_LIMIT` is now a depth bound (~511) rather than a pass budget; in-place would have resolved that chain in about one pass. Capacity for the 20,000-instance target is unaffected (`capacityFor` = exact pin bits × 1.25 + 16, `src/core/net.ts:90-98`, so 20,000 two-input gates → 75,016 slots, and `alloc` can never reject a validated graph); the real cost is throughput, O(depth × instances) per settle after an input/edge change instead of O(instances). Acceptable for this phase — the deepest reference solution is depth 4, the capacity test is depth 1 (`test/core/net.test.ts:46-58`), and every storage element breaks the path so tick-driven CPU-style circuits stay shallow — but Phase 1 should evaluate the acyclic prefix in the topological order `delayOf` already computes and iterate only the feedback cores.
- **`inputBase` semantics: safe for Task 6.** The plan's `bindLevelIo` reads a level output as `net.inputBase('OUT.in')` (`plan:2464-2472`) and drives inputs as `net.outputBase('IN_<pin>.out')` (`plan:2486-2490`). With the brief's own-slot version, `OUT.in`'s own slot is never written by anything once the pin is wired, so `readOutput` could only ever return 0 — the driver-slot semantics (`src/core/net.ts:183`) is load-bearing for the next task, and `runRow`/the script branch settle before ticking, so the supported drive path works (`plan:2614,2650`). "Unwired reads 0" is preserved by the identity `drive` plus the zeroed table (`src/core/net.ts:155-156`, `src/core/signal.ts:104-106`), and both directions are exercised (`test/core/net.test.ts:96-104,189-218`). One caveat Task 6 must respect: writing through the `inputBase` of a *wired* pin targets the driver's output slot and is overwritten by that driver on the next sweep — Task 6 only writes via `outputBase`, so it is safe.
- **Unstable fixture: correct**, and identical in shape to the Lead's corrected plan fixture (`test/core/net.test.ts:106-118` vs `plan:2269-2276`): free NAND inputs tied to `const_on`, so each gate inverts and the loop cannot find a fixed point from the reset state. Caveat: the test's rationale "the loop has no stable state" (`test/core/net.test.ts:107-108`) is mathematically false — `(1,0)`/`(0,1)` are fixed points, which is why detection depends on the zero-initialised table; the plan resets before every row/attempt (`plan:2607,2648`) so classification is deterministic, but a three-inverter ring (no fixed point at all) would be the rigorous fixture.

### Strengths

- The two consequential deviations are both *forced* by the plan's own code, and the implementer proved it with a RED run rather than asserting it; my independent hand traces agree with both conclusions (`plan:2262-2281`, `plan:2450-2497`).
- `settle()`'s escape hatch for defs that write nothing is the mechanism that makes level I/O work at all, and it is precisely scoped (`src/core/net.ts:335,343`), with a test on both the drive and the read side (`test/core/net.test.ts:176-218`).
- `delayOf` is genuinely linear, terminates on cycles without throwing, degrades to cost 0 for unknown defs instead of exploding out of a metrics function (`src/core/net.ts:419-421`), and returns the value the plan expects for its own reference solution (`plan:2966`).
- Change detection was moved from value-form equality to bits with the reason written down, and the wide-pin test is a true discrimination test rather than a restatement (`src/core/net.ts:286-301`, `test/core/net.test.ts:240-265`).
- The capacity deviation was necessary and is derived rather than guessed: the plan's "fits in the default 65,536 slots with room to spare" (`plan:458-459`) is false for the stated 20,000-instance budget, and the ledger already asked for an explicit capacity (`progress.md:161-167`).
- Test quality is high overall: real circuits, real values, no implementation restating; the strongest cases are the 2^30-path diamond (`test/core/net.test.ts:311-330`), the hold-through-settle timing test (`test/core/net.test.ts:146-175`), and the `>65,536`-slot capacity test (`test/core/net.test.ts:46-58`).
- `pnpm build`'s cleanliness covers the test file too, since `tsconfig.json:17` includes `test` — so "build clean" is real type coverage, not just `src`.

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)
None. No defect found that is reachable with Phase 0's pins (grep confirms no pin wider than 1 exists in `src/` or the plan) or that violates a mandated invariant.

#### Important (Should Fix)
None reachable in Phase 0. The two real forward-looking risks are filed as Minor 1 and Minor 2 with their concrete Phase-1 triggers, because neither can affect a 1-bit-pin, depth-≤-10 circuit.

#### Minor (Nice to Have)
1. `src/core/net.ts:266-274` — `#readInputs` reads `width` bits *contiguously* from `drive[base]`, bypassing the per-bit drive map. Wrong whenever the driver pin is narrower than the target input pin: e.g. a 4-bit output into an 8-bit input reads 4 bits of a neighbouring pin instead of the intended zeros (`drive` maps those bits to the target's own zero slots, which this loop ignores). Unreachable in Phase 0; silently wrong the moment Phase 1's wide `maker`/register ports land, and silent data corruption is worse than a throw. Fix: gather bit-by-bit (`slots[this.#drive[base + bit]]`) or point over-wide bits at a shared zero slot and mask to the driver width. The same assumption sits behind `inputBase`-based reads with a spec width (`plan:2467`).
2. `src/core/net.ts:317-356` (+ `src/core/net.ts:7`) — `SETTLE_LIMIT` is now a combinational *depth* cap: a legal acyclic circuit of depth ≥ 512 raises `UnstableCircuitError` whose message asserts "combinational feedback loop" (`src/core/errors.ts:18`) and whose `blame` lists everything (`src/core/net.ts:352-355`). 3. `src/core/net.ts:352-355` vs `src/core/errors.ts:13` — `blame` is the whole circuit while its own doc says it is "for highlighting the culprit", and the test only asserts `toContain` (`test/core/net.test.ts:130`), which is trivially true when everything is blamed. Fix: reuse a Kahn pass and blame the instances that never reach in-degree 0 (plus their downstream cone), then assert set equality.
4. `test/core/net.test.ts:297-310` — the `delayOf` storage-break test cannot fail under the brief's source-only version, because every Phase 0 storage def costs 0 (`src/core/defs/index.ts:132,156`), so it does not pin the two-directional break its comment claims (`src/core/net.ts:432`). Fix: a custom registry with `{ sequential: true, cost: 2 }` — shipped code returns 1, the brief's version 3.
5. `src/core/net.ts:359-384` — `tick()`'s precondition is undocumented: it samples whatever the table holds, so a caller that writes inputs and ticks without an intervening `settle()` samples unpropagated values. The plan always settles first (`plan:2614,2650`) and each `tick()` ends with a settle, so this is inert today. Fix: one sentence in the doc comment, or settle-on-dirty.
6. `src/core/net.ts:363-365` vs `test/core/net.test.ts:146-175` — the "two storage elements in series shift one stage per tick" guarantee has no test; only a single `delay_line` is covered. Fix: chain two `delay_line`s and assert the second lags the first by exactly one tick.
7. `src/core/net.ts:286-297` — `#holds` treats bits ≥ 32 of a *number* value as 0, while `setPort`'s number path wraps shifts mod 32 (`src/core/signal.ts:76-80`, already ledgered at `progress.md:161-163`); a >32-bit port written as a number can therefore never compare equal and would be misreported as unstable after 512 sweeps. 8. `src/core/net.ts:118-119,189,210-217` — the `SignalTable` lives on the netlist while `#state` lives on the `Simulation`, so a second `new Simulation(net, registry)` over one netlist silently shares signals; the plan creates one per netlist (`plan:2554-2557,2693-2694`) and `runRow` resets per row, so it is inert. 9. `test/core/net.test.ts:107-108` — fixture comment claims the loop has "no stable state"; false for a two-inverter ring (see adjudication). Fix the comment and add a three-inverter ring test, which is unstable under *any* starting state.
10. `src/core/net.ts:455-460` — the cycle comment mentions only instances inside a loop; nodes downstream of a loop also never reach in-degree 0 and so contribute no depth. Cosmetic, since such circuits fail the settle check anyway; worth one clause in the comment.

**Task quality:** Approved
**Reasoning:** Every mandated invariant is met and both consequential deviations are correct and demonstrably required by the plan's own corrected fixtures and by Task 6's `bindLevelIo` code, which I verified against the plan source rather than the report. No Phase-0-reachable defect exists; the listed Minors are latent (multi-bit pins do not exist yet in this phase) or coverage gaps, and should ride along with the first wide-port/CPU work rather than block this commit.

Task 5's review is solid—it validated both deviations as correct and necessary. The reviewer flagged the delayed verdict test as weak and noted I should add assertions for depth 511 and a two-delay_line chain test. I'll record these as deferred items and move forward with Task 6, which is where the real work is.

Before dispatching Task 6, I'm checking the reviewer's flagged risk on `#readInputs`: the implementation reads `width` bits contiguously from the drive map, which bypasses per-bit routing. For Phase 0 with all width-1 pins this works fine, but Phase 1's multi-bit widths would need to honor the per-bit map instead. It's a deferred item with a clear trigger—Phase 1 wide ports—so I'll note it and proceed.

Now I need to review Task 4, dispatch it, update the ledger, and then move to Task 6. Let me batch the Task 4 review dispatch with the ledger updates since they're independent.

{"description": "Review Task 4 (graph model)", "prompt": "You are reviewing one task's implementation: first whether it matches its requirements, then whether it is well-built. This is a task-scoped gate, not a merge review — a broad whole-branch review happens separately after all tasks are complete.

Work from: `D:\Documents\turing-complete`

## What Was Requested

Read the task brief: `D:\Documents\turing-complete\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase0\task-4-brief.md`

Global constraints from the spec/design that bind this task:
- **Zero runtime dependencies.** Nothing may be added to `package.json`.
- Instance ids are `i1`, `i2`, …; wire ids are `w1`, `w2`, …; `nextId` returns the next free numeric suffix (`nextId('i', [{id:'i1'},{id:'i3'}]) === 'i4'`, `nextId('i', []) === 'i1'`).
- `validateGraph` **returns issues and never throws**. `severity: 'error'` is reserved for a circuit that is meaningless: `unknown-def`, `unknown-instance` (a wire pointing at a missing instance), `unknown-port` (a wire pointing at a missing port), `multiple-drivers` (two wires on one input pin). `severity: 'warning'` covers `dangling-input` (unwired input, which reads 0) and `feedback-loop`.
- **A feedback loop is a warning, not an error** — storage elements make legitimate loops and the player is often mid-edit. Combinational loops become fatal only in the simulator, which raises `UnstableCircuitError` when a circuit fails to settle.

content.text:
### Spec Compliance
- ✅ **Spec compliant.** Every pinned interface, severity, and behaviour checks out against the diff; the report's single deviation is a test fixture, already ratified, and it is the correct half of the brief to change.
- ✅ **Unknown def never reaches `registry.get`** — exactly one call site, [graph.ts:178](src/core/graph.ts#L178), guarded by `registry.has(inst.def)` in the same expression; every instance is resolved once into `defs` ([graph.ts:189](src/core/graph.ts#L189)) and the wire walk reads only that cache ([graph.ts:206](src/core/graph.ts#L206), [graph.ts:223-224](src/core/graph.ts#L223-L224)). A bogus def yields an issue, not a throw. Checked the consumer: [net.ts:93-94](src/core/net.ts#L93-L94) calls `registry.get(inst.def)` **unguarded** in `capacityFor` on the stated assumption that `validateGraph` already rejected unknown defs — that assumption holds precisely because `unknown-def` is an error and `compile` throws first ([net.ts:109-112](src/core/net.ts#L109-L112)).
- ✅ **Severities exact, code by code** — `unknown-def` error [graph.ts:180-181](src/core/graph.ts#L180-L181); `unknown-instance` error [graph.ts:197-198](src/core/graph.ts#L197-L198); `unknown-port` error on the `from` side [graph.ts:210-211](src/core/graph.ts#L210-L211) and the `to` side [graph.ts:223-224](src/core/graph.ts#L223-L224); `multiple-drivers` error [graph.ts:246-247](src/core/graph.ts#L246-L247); `feedback-loop` warning [graph.ts:302-303](src/core/graph.ts#L302-L303); `dangling-input` warning [graph.ts:317-318](src/core/graph.ts#L317-L318). No error/warning is inverted. Checked consumer filtering: [net.ts:109-112](src/core/net.ts#L109-L112) takes `severity === 'error'` as fatal and accepts warnings, so an unwired input cannot block a level pass.
- ✅ **`cloneGraph` deep-copies custom-component bodies** — instances + `params` [graph.ts:138](src/core/graph.ts#L138), both wire ends [graph.ts:139](src/core/graph.ts#L139), `id`/`name`/`inputs`/`outputs`/recursive `body` [graph.ts:140-146](src/core/graph.ts#L140-L146), with recursive `body: cloneGraph(c.body)` at [graph.ts:145](src/core/graph.ts#L145) so nested bodies are covered too. Independence is structural in **both** directions (every nested object is rebuilt; no reference is shared), and the copy→original direction is asserted at [graph.test.ts:37-69](test/core/graph.test.ts#L37-L69).
- ✅ **`removeInstance` drops attached wires; `disconnect` leaves instances alone** — [graph.ts:113-114](src/core/graph.ts#L113-L114) filters wires by `from.inst` *and* `to.inst`; [graph.ts:128](src/core/graph.ts#L128) touches only `g.wires`. Asserted at [graph.test.ts:71-80](test/core/graph.test.ts#L71-L80) and [graph.test.ts:82-90](test/core/graph.test.ts#L82-L90).
- ✅ **Loop detection is genuinely iterative and terminates** — explicit `{id, next}` frame stack [graph.ts:266-297](src/core/graph.ts#L266-L297), no self-call; a node is pushed at most once (GREY set on push [graph.ts:287-289](src/core/graph.ts#L287-L289), BLACK on pop [graph.ts:294-295](src/core/graph.ts#L294-L295)), so the scan is O(V+E) on a large acyclic graph. Back-edge test `c === GREY` [graph.ts:291-293](src/core/graph.ts#L291-L293) is sound because GREY ⇔ on-stack in this loop. `adjacency.get(...)!` [graph.ts:280](src/core/graph.ts#L280) and `stack[...]!` are provably non-null: every instance id is an adjacency key ([graph.ts:277](src/core/graph.ts#L277)) and frames only come from those keys — no crash path.
- ✅ **`multiple-drivers` carries the right `inst`/`port`** — key built at [graph.ts:234](src/core/graph.ts#L234) in the consumer's own `${inst.id}.${pin.id}` convention ([net.ts:126](src/core/net.ts#L126), [net.ts:132](src/core/net.ts#L132)), recovered at [graph.ts:244](src/core/graph.ts#L244); asserted directly at [graph.test.ts:171-183](test/core/graph.test.ts#L171-L183) (`inst === c.id`, `port === 'a'`, exactly one issue).
- ✅ **Zero runtime dependencies** — [graph.ts:1](src/core/graph.ts#L1) is `import type` only (erased at compile time); the diff touches only `src/core/graph.ts` and `test/core/graph.test.ts`, no `package.json`.
- ✅ **`nextId` contract** — max numeric suffix + 1, non-numeric suffixes ignored ([graph.ts:89-96](src/core/graph.ts#L89-L96)); `i1/i3 → i4` and `[] → i1` asserted at [graph.test.ts:92-95](test/core/graph.test.ts#L92-L95).
- ✅ **`emptyGraph` optionality** — `level` is omitted rather than set to `undefined` ([graph.ts:80-81](src/core/graph.ts#L80-L81)), which is the only shape that survives `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`.
- ✅ **The amended fixture is genuinely well-formed** — checked the defs it relies on: `const_off` exists, has **no inputs** and one `out` ([defs/index.ts:75](src/core/defs/index.ts#L75), [defs/index.ts:39-51](src/core/defs/index.ts#L39-L51)); `nand` is `a,b → out`, `not` is `a → out` ([defs/index.ts:81-82](src/core/defs/index.ts#L81-L82), [defs/index.ts:18-22](src/core/defs/index.ts#L18-L22)). All three inputs are driven exactly once and the graph is acyclic, so `toHaveLength(0)` at [graph.test.ts:114](test/core/graph.test.ts#L114) is satisfiable. Nothing here was weakened.
- ⚠️ **Cannot verify from diff:** the reported `15/15`, `56/56`, and `tsc --noEmit && vite build` clean outputs — not re-run, per instruction. The controller should confirm from the Lead's run; nothing I checked statically contradicts them. The report's "recursive would blow the stack" claim *is* independently substantiated below.

### Strengths
- The severity contract is documented on both sides of the module boundary: [graph.ts:79-86](src/core/graph.ts#L79-L86) and [net.ts:104-106](src/core/net.ts#L104-L106) say the same thing, so a future edit to one is visibly a change to the other's assumption.
- Error handling is by guard, not by catch: one guarded lookup, a per-instance def cache the wire walk consults, and no `try/catch` hiding a real throw. Checked [registry.ts:83-85](src/core/registry.ts#L83-L85) — `get` throws `unknown component: ${id}` and [registry.ts:88](src/core/registry.ts#L88) confirms `has` is the correct non-throwing probe, so the gating claim in the report is true rather than convenient.
- The four added tests are **legitimate hardening, not scope creep**: each pins a distinct global constraint the brief's ten tests left uncovered — warning-non-fatal ([graph.test.ts:117](test/core/graph.test.ts#L117)), the `registry.get` throw path from the wire walk ([graph.test.ts:139](test/core/graph.test.ts#L139)), custom-component deep copy ([graph.test.ts:37](test/core/graph.test.ts#L37)), non-recursion ([graph.test.ts:196](test/core/graph.test.ts#L196)). None restates the implementation, and **none asserts something trivially true**; the closest is [graph.test.ts:129](test/core/graph.test.ts#L129), which overlaps [graph.test.ts:126](test/core/graph.test.ts#L126) but genuinely asserts the `severity` field rather than inferring it from the code list. [graph.test.ts:139](test/core/graph.test.ts#L139) would catch a regression to `registry.get(inst.def)` inside the wire walk, and [graph.test.ts:55-68](test/core/graph.test.ts#L55-L68) would fail on any aliasing.
- The 50k test is a real guard, not a claim about a hypothetical implementation: I measured V8's max recursion depth on this machine (`node -e` counter) at **12,477 frames**, so a 50,000-node descent is ~4× past the limit and any recursive rewrite fails the test. It also exercises the deep-descent path specifically, since the cycle closes only after ~50k frames ([graph.test.ts:200-208](test/core/graph.test.ts#L200-L208)).

#### Critical (Must Fix)
None.

#### Important (Should Fix)
None. Every pinned requirement, the severity split, the non-throwing contract, and the `compile` consumer contract ([net.ts:109-112](src/core/net.ts#L109-L112), [net.ts:93-94](src/core/net.ts#L93-L94)) hold as specified; the remaining items are quality and forward-risk notes, not defects that make this task untrustworthy.

1. [graph.ts:234](src/core/graph.ts#L234) + [graph.ts:244](src/core/graph.ts#L244) — the `drivenInputs` key is a concatenated string recovered with `key.split('.')`, so a caller-supplied instance id containing a dot (`addInstance(g, def, x, y, id?)` accepts any string, [graph.ts:98](src/core/graph.ts#L98)) makes `multiple-drivers` report the wrong `inst` (id `a.b` → `inst: 'a'`, `port: 'b'`). 2. 3. [graph.ts:164-347](src/core/graph.ts#L164-L347) — `validateGraph` never descends into `customComponents[].body`, so a bogus def or a combinational loop *inside* a body is unreported. Not a Phase 0 hazard: [net.ts:22-23](src/core/net.ts#L22-L23) states Phase 0 does not expand custom components, so no body ever reaches a registry lookup. Fix belongs to whichever task first compiles a body (recurse, or validate each body on instantiation).
4. [graph.ts:136-147](src/core/graph.ts#L136-L147) — clone **fidelity** is untested, only non-aliasing: [graph.test.ts:27-35](test/core/graph.test.ts#L27-L35) and [graph.test.ts:37-69](test/core/graph.test.ts#L37-L69) assert independence but nothing asserts the copy carries equal values, `level`, or `params`. Report self-review item 5 lists `level` preservation as "verified" with no test in the diff — the controller should read that as a manual probe, not coverage.
5. [graph.ts:98-109](src/core/graph.ts#L98-L109),[graph.ts:121-124](src/core/graph.ts#L121-L124) push into `g.instances`/`g.wires` while [graph.ts:113-114](src/core/graph.ts#L113-L114),[graph.ts:128](src/core/graph.ts#L128) **replace** those arrays. 6. [graph.ts:183-184](src/core/graph.ts#L183-L184) — duplicate instance ids are undiagnosed (`byId`/`defs` are last-wins), so two instances can collapse into one and the dangling scan can report the same pin twice. **Task quality:** Approved
**Reasoning:** Every pinned behaviour is verified in the diff — the guarded registry lookup, the exact code-by-code severity split, warning-only `dangling-input`/`feedback-loop`, the iterative O(V+E) scan, direction-independent wire removal, and a custom-component-recursive `cloneGraph` — and the consumer contract in `compile` ([net.ts:109-112](src/core/net.ts#L109-L112)) holds; the four added tests are genuine hardening, none tautological, with the 50k guard independently substantiated against V8's measured 12,477-frame limit (report's test counts not re-run, per instruction). Tasks 4 and 5 are complete, so I'm moving on to Task 6 with the existing codebase as my base. I need to be careful with the test fixtures and runChecks handling to make sure everything integrates properly.

The inputBase semantics shift the behavior — Task 6's bindLevelIo reads level output from the driver slot and drives inputs through outputBase, which the plan already accounts for. The reviewer flagged that runChecks needs to catch UnstableCircuitError properly, and I need to clarify the distinction between createSim errors and settle-time errors now that Simulation construction doesn't settle like it did in the brief's version. The storage element contract is also in place. I'm double-checking that Simulation's constructor doesn't settle in the shipped version, which changes when validation errors surface compared to what the plan assumes.

It is your requirements, with the exact values to use verbatim. Follow its steps in order.

## Context

We are building a from-scratch replica of the puzzle game *Turing Complete*: players wire logic gates out of NAND gates and work up to a CPU. This is Phase 0, a vertical slice covering chapter 1 (12 levels).

Done and green (full suite 75/75, `pnpm build` clean):
- Task 1 — skeleton (Vite 8 + Vitest 5 + TS 5.9).
- Task 2 — `src/core/signal.ts`: fixed-capacity signal table, `PortValue`.
- Task 3 — `src/core/registry.ts` + `src/core/defs/index.ts`: 15 component defs.
- Task 4 — `src/core/graph.ts`: editable document model + `validateGraph`.
- Task 5 — `src/core/net.ts` + `src/core/errors.ts`: the simulator.

This task turns a circuit into a pass/fail verdict against a level's declared tests. Task 7 grades it; Tasks 8–9 author the 12 real chapters; Task 11 shows the failures in the UI.

Work from: `D:\Documents\turing-complete` (git repo, branch `master`).

## Interfaces from earlier tasks you must use (the brief predates some of these — trust this section where they differ)

- `Simulation.read(base, width)` / `write(base, width, value)` address **slots**.
- **`net.inputBase(key)` returns the DRIVER slot, not the pin's own slot.** This was a deliberate Task 5 fix: with the pin's own slot, `net.inputBase('OUT.in')` could only ever read 0 once the pin was wired, which would make every level unpassable. So reading a level output via `net.inputBase('OUT.in')` is correct. Conversely, **writing** through the `inputBase` of a *wired* pin targets the driver's output slot and is overwritten on the next sweep — so drive level *inputs* through `net.outputBase('IN_<pin>.out')` and never write through `inputBase`.
- **`new Simulation(net, registry)` does not settle.** The `UnstableCircuitError` therefore surfaces at the first `io.reset()` or `io.sim.settle()`, not at construction. Your error handling must therefore wrap the settle/settle-driving calls, not just the construction.
- `ComponentDef.evaluate`'s signature is `(inputs, outputs, state, ctx)` with `state` a **required** third parameter typed `Uint8Array | undefined`. If you call a def's `evaluate` directly in a test, pass `undefined` for combinational defs.
- `compile(graph, registry)` throws `CircuitValidationError` on **error**-severity issues and **accepts warnings**. An unwired input is a warning and reads 0 — a circuit with an unwired input must still be evaluatable.
- `validateGraph` returns issues and never throws; `registry.get(id)` **throws** on an unknown id, so guard with `registry.has(id)`.

The brief's unstable-feedback-loop fixture was wrong and the Lead has already corrected it in the plan. **Cross-coupled NANDs with unwired free inputs are a STABLE fixed point** (`nand(x, 0) === 1` for every `x` — a perfectly good SR latch), so they never oscillate. The corrected fixture ties both free inputs high via a `const_on`, making each gate an inverter. Use the corrected version from the brief.

## Design decisions already made (do not re-litigate)

- **Level I/O binds by a dedicated plumbing part, not by pin name.** `level_input` / `level_output` are in `BASE_DEFS` (`category: 'level'`, `cost: 0`, `hidden: true`). An instance whose id is `IN_<pinId>` supplies that level input; an instance whose id is `OUT` (single output) or `OUT_<pinId>` (multi-output) mirrors that level output. Pin names come from the **component def**, so they cannot be used to bind — that is why this convention exists.
- **`bindLevelIo` reads and writes at the width the level declares** (`pin.width`), not a hard-coded 1. All Phase 0 pins are width 1, but Task 9's level 12 has four 1-bit outputs and later phases have wide pins, so the width must come from the spec.
- **A `truth-table` check with no rows is a hard failure** (`reason: 'missing-rows'`), not a pass. An earlier draft generated "empty outputs" rows and then compared nothing, so every circuit ever built passed. This is one of the most important behaviours in the task.
- **One compilation per check, reused for every row.** Compiling per row would re-run `validateGraph` and reallocate the signal table hundreds of times per level.
- `CheckFailure.reason` is a union that includes `'missing-rows'` (new) alongside `'mismatch' | 'unstable' | 'invalid' | 'missing-io'`.

- node: `C:\Users\ME\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\node\bin\node.exe`
- pnpm: `C:\Users\ME\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\pnpm\bin\pnpm.mjs`
- Invoke as: `& "<node path>" "<pnpm path>" test` — bare `pnpm` on PATH is broken.
- Vitest's global environment is `node`; do not add `environmentMatchGlobs` (removed in Vitest 5).
- Run the focused test file while iterating; run the full suite and `pnpm build` once before committing.

## Global Constraints (bind this task)

- **Zero runtime dependencies.** Nothing may be added to `package.json`.
- Combinational loops must raise `UnstableCircuitError`, never hang.
- Level checks must never throw at the caller: a broken, empty, or unstable circuit produces a **failed outcome**, not an exception. `grade()` in Task 7 relies on this.
- Source is UTF-8; code comments in English.
- Do not copy anything from the original game.
- Commits are in English, format `type: summary`.

## If the brief's code cannot satisfy the brief's own test

This has happened in three of the five preceding tasks. When it does: decide which side expresses the *intent* the brief states in prose, implement that side, keep the strong assertion if you can, and **report the conflict prominently** with the RED evidence. Do not quietly weaken an assertion, and do not quietly change a mandated behaviour.

## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

Do all of this task's work yourself. Never spawn a subagent, and never spawn a reviewer to check your work — a fresh reviewer is dispatched against your diff after you report. Self-review means reading your own diff.

Write your full report to `D:\Documents\turing-complete\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase0\task-6-report.md`:
- What you implemented
- What you tested and the results
- **TDD Evidence**: RED (command, failing output, why that expectation failed) and GREEN (command, passing output)
- Files changed
- Self-review findings
- Any issues or concerns

Then reply with ONLY (under 15 lines):
- **Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT
- Commits created (short SHA + subject)
- One-line test summary
- Your concerns, if any
- The report file path", "run_in_background": false}

Global constraints from the spec/design that bind this task:
- **Zero runtime dependencies.**
- **Level checks must never throw at the caller.** A broken, empty, or unstable circuit produces a *failed outcome*, not an exception. `grade()` in Task 7 depends on this.
- **A `truth-table` check with no rows is a hard failure** (`reason: 'missing-rows'`), not a pass. An earlier draft generated "empty outputs" rows, compared nothing, and therefore passed every circuit ever built. This is one of the most important behaviours in the phase.
- `CheckFailure.reason` is a union including `'missing-rows'` alongside `'mismatch' | 'unstable' | 'invalid' | 'missing-io'`.
- **Level I/O binds by instance id, with the pin name coming from the level spec**: `IN_<pinId>` supplies a level input; `OUT` (single output) or `OUT_<pinId>` (multi-output) mirrors a level output. - **`bindLevelIo` reads and writes at the width the level declares** (`pin.width`), not a hard-coded 1.
- **One compilation per check, reused for every row** — compiling per row would re-run `validateGraph` and reallocate the signal table hundreds of times per level.
- `compile()` throws `CircuitValidationError` on error-severity graph issues and **accepts warnings**; an unwired input is a warning and reads 0.
- `new Simulation(net, registry)` does not settle, so `UnstableCircuitError` surfaces at the first `reset()`/`settle()`, not at construction. Error handling must wrap the settle-driving calls.
- `net.inputBase(key)` returns the **driver** slot (a Task 5 fix, load-bearing: the pin's own slot would always read 0). Writes must go through `net.outputBase`.
