- ⚠️ **"the brief fixes its kind, its 256 rounds and its fixed-seed rule"** (`batch3.ts:275-277`): `task-10-brief.md` fixes the checker kind and 256 rounds; it states no seed rule. If "the brief" means the phase plan, fine; against the brief in the review package, the seed discipline is convention, not a brief requirement.

- ⚠️ **Measured numbers quoted in prose.** The per-opcode counts (31/30/31/33/34/31/35/31), the eight first-failing rounds, the alternatives' 112/78/104/54/35 and the level-27 breakdown (497 + 171 = 668) are not verifiable from the diff. Every one of them is re-measured by an assertion at run time (`ch2-batch3.test.ts:1074`, `:1097`, `:1161-1240`, `:800`), so a wrong printed value fails the suite — but I did not re-run it.

- ⚠️ **Chapter-1 metrics are not pinned to targets.** `ch1-part1.test.ts:240` and `ch1-part2.test.ts:218` use `metrics` only in a failure message (they assert `stars === 3`). A chapter-1 score that *fell* while staying inside its target would be invisible; my item-8 conclusion for chapter 1 is structural (no existing price changed), not test-backed.

- ⚠️ **Playability is not covered by this diff.** `batch3.ts:83` records that `ch2/index.ts` still lists batch 1 alone, so levels 23–27 are reachable only through their own test; the assembly task will also need the five ids added to `level-buildability.test.ts`'s `REFERENCE_SOLUTIONS` map.

### Strengths

- The one-hot contract is asserted three independent ways (def pins/behaviour, level truth tables, hand-written literals in `registry.test.ts`), with an explicit "not `sel`" assertion from `sel = 2` up — the failure mode this item exists to catch (a wire wearing a decoder's pins) is hunted rather than assumed away.
- `threeStar` is asserted **equal** to its reference's measured metrics for all five levels (`ch2-batch3.test.ts:800-807`), the strongest available form of "the target is the reference's own metrics"; the alternatives block then measures what each target separates, so the comparative claims in the data comments are measurements, not prose.
- Opcode coverage is proven, not hoped for: per-opcode counts from the level's own literal seed, one hand-picked vector per opcode, and eight one-opcode-broken variants whose failure round must be a round of the broken opcode.
- The gate-cost derivation is a real derivation (`wide.ts:900`) cross-checked against both level targets (1 and 27) instead of asserted, and it is explicitly called a construction rather than a minimum.
- The category assertion was fixed by making the expectation track the module's literal registration tuples — verified non-tautological by reading the three tuples — with the `const8` exception stated as an assertion (`defs-wide.test.ts:271`) rather than filtered out silently.
- The pre-existing defect-class guard was **widened**, not worked around: `CH2_BATCH3` joined the `SHIPPED` walk and `decoder1`/`decoder3` became non-vacuity anchors (`registry.test.ts:634, 654-655`), so the walk cannot pass while the hole stands.
- No engine behaviour changed: the defs commit adds a generator plus literal tuples; the levels commit touches level data and tests only, and the five levels are pure data as required.

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)

None.

#### Important (Should Fix)

1. **`batch3.ts:57-58` claims level 25 is the only level answered by a part it offers — level 26's own reward `decoder3` answers level 26 the same way, and nothing records it.** The header says "the one part a level in this batch both offers and is answered by is level 25's OWN reward, `decoder1`". But level 26's palette lists `decoder3` (`batch3.ts:535`, its own reward at `:542`), and `decoder3`'s pins are exactly level 26's I/O (`sel:3 → out:8`, `wide.ts:925-926`): one drop-in scores `gate 27` (equal to the target at `batch3.ts:541`), `delay 1` (target 3) and `tick 0` → three stars, bypassing the "share the low decode" lesson exactly as ruling 3 describes for `neg8`. Level 25's own case is recorded in its comment (`batch3.ts:462-472`) and measured by a test (`ch2-batch3.test.ts:1353`); level 26 has neither — its comment's palette paragraph (`batch3.ts:~505-510`) explains only why `splitter`/`maker` are offered. Why it matters: this batch's whole method is "measure the seam and record it", and the sentence that was added to record it is factually wrong about its own batch, which is how a second trivialisation stays invisible. Fix: correct the header sentence to name both cases, and add the level-26 equivalent of the level-25 paragraph and measurement (grading a `decoder3` instance against `ch2-26-3-bit-decoder` and comparing `metrics` with `L26.threeStar`). Offering `decoder3` is *not* the defect — the binding rule deliberately offers a level its own reward — so recording is the fix; withdrawing it from level 26's palette is the alternative if the controller prefers to protect that lesson, and is permitted by "may offer".

#### Minor (Nice to Have)

2. **`wide.ts:843` uses the operator the implementation warns against.** The section note says "The value published is `1 << sel`", while `createDecoderDef`'s own comment (`wide.ts:914-917`) says "`2 ** sel` and not `1 << sel`: `<<` converts through int32, so at a 5-bit select bit 31 would come out negative". Same file, two notations, one of them the rejected one — write `2 ** sel` (or "bit `sel` high") in the section note.
3. **`wide.ts:868` rationale is not true of `number`.** "`2 ** 5 = 32` is the widest value a `number` carries exactly" — JavaScript integers are exact to 2^53; the real ceiling is the project's 32-bit port carrier (`MAX_WIDE_WIDTH = 32`, `wide.ts:89`; `fitsWidth` special-cases width ≥ 32, `src/core/signal.ts:16-19`). The conclusion (w = 5, out = 32 bits) is right; reword the sentence.
4. **`test/core/defs-wide.test.ts:265` trades away a direction the old literal list checked.** The expectation now comes from the module tuples, so "every wide def has a row in this file's contract tables" is no longer asserted: a future family member added to a tuple would pass this test with no tabulated pin/price contract here. Covered today (the decoders' contract is explicit in `registry.test.ts:501-556`), and the report states the trade, but a one-line assertion that each wide id appears in some contract table — or a note naming where each family's contract lives — keeps the file's own promise.
5. **`batch3.ts:481-482` tells the player to drop `decoder2` in, and no palette offers it.** The ruled wording and the deliberate palette decision are both recorded (`batch3.ts:450-460`, `ch2-batch3.test.ts:1350`), so this is only the player-visible seam: the brief names a part that cannot be selected in this chapter.
6. **`batch3.ts:497-500` puts a design fact in the SOURCED half.** Level 26's SOURCED clause says "the same generator as level 25 one width up (… `decoder3` is `createDecoderDef(3)`)". The generator is this replica's mechanism; keeping it in the SOURCED sentence blurs the split the batch is otherwise careful about. Move the `createDecoderDef(3)` clause to AUTHORED.
7. **`registry.test.ts:501` asserts names only for `decoder1`/`decoder3`.** `decoder2`'s pins, price and behaviour are covered by the generator loop (`registry.test.ts:559`) but its generated name (`2 位解码器` / `2-Bit Decoder`) is not asserted anywhere; one extra row in `ROWS` covers it.

### Part 2: Code Quality

- **Structure.** The decoder family sits between the operators and the storage family with a section note in the file's own idiom (`wide.ts:822-841`, mirroring `THE STORAGE FAMILY (task 4)`), and is registered the way `wide.ts` registers its other families: a generator (`createDecoderDef`), a literal width list (`DECODER_WIDTHS`), a literal id tuple (`DECODER_DEF_IDS`), and `DECODER_DEFS = DECODER_WIDTHS.map(createDecoderDef)` — the same generator + literal-tuple shape as `WIDE_DEF_IDS`/`createWideDefs` and `WIDE_STORAGE_DEF_IDS`/`WIDE_STORAGE_DEFS`, with the two lists pinned to each other by a test (`registry.test.ts:559-566`). Not being a `createWideDefs` product is correct and documented: that generator forces one width on every pin (`wide.ts:822-836`), and a decoder's pins must differ. Refusing out-of-range widths rather than clamping diverges from `clampWidth` (`wide.ts:100-103`); the justification (clamping would silently hand back a part with a different pin shape) is sound, so the divergence is deliberate rather than an inconsistency.
- **Should it have been a `params.width` knob?** No — I verified the premise independently: `src/core/net.ts:98-99` is `inst.params.width ?? pin.width`, and the file's own doc at `net.ts:88` says `params.width` covers every pin of that instance; `net.ts:305` additionally joins a driver to a sink by `Math.min(driverWidth, sinkWidth)`, which is also why level 25's 8-bit `maker` into a 2-bit level output is legal. Ruling 1 is right, and the follow-up's replacement of the brief text is the correct resolution.
- **Are the comments load-bearing or noise?** Load-bearing, and each claim I spot-checked against the code is either a measurement or flagged as arithmetic (`batch3.ts:567-571` and `:571-580` do label the level-27 alternative as arithmetic rather than a measurement). The cost of the volume is that a stale claim survives review — which is precisely what issue 1 is. The module header earns its length by carrying cross-level facts (palette rule, not-joined status, reward-def seam) that no single level comment can own.
- **Do the tests verify behaviour rather than restate data?** Mostly behaviour: decoder tables written out by hand and checked against `evaluate`; one-hotness and the "not `sel`" reading; the category assertion derived from independent tuples; opcode coverage and break-one-opcode variants; counterexample failure records recomputed from pure functions; palette walks in both directions with the storage family asserted unreachable. The one restatement is `hands out the parts the brief assigns to each level` (`ch2-batch3.test.ts:457`), which is legitimate pinning of the brief's unlock column, and the SOURCED/AUTHORED marker test (`:488`) is a string presence check — weak by nature, which is why the substantive check for it is reading the comments, as this review did.

### Assessment

**Task quality:** Needs fixes

**Reasoning:** The five levels, the decoder family and the corrected level-25 brief are in substance correct — one-hot decoders verified against the defs, 1/10/27 derived and cross-checked, targets asserted equal to their own references' measurements, counterexamples graded-and-wrong, opcode coverage measured rather than assumed, and no existing score moveable by the diff; the single defect is that `batch3.ts:57-58` states level 25 is the only level answered by a part it offers, when level 26's own reward `decoder3` does the same and the batch neither records nor measures it.

Level 25's own case is recorded in its comment (`batch3.ts:462-472`) and measured by a test (`ch2-batch3.test.ts:1353`); level 26 has neither — its comment's palette paragraph (`batch3.ts:~505-510`) explains only why `splitter`/`maker` are offered. Why it matters: this batch's whole method is "measure the seam and record it", and the sentence that was added to record it is factually wrong about its own batch, which is how a second trivialisation stays invisible. Fix: correct the header sentence to name both cases, and add the level-26 equivalent of the level-25 paragraph and measurement (grading a `decoder3` instance against `ch2-26-3-bit-decoder` and comparing `metrics` with `L26.threeStar`). Offering `decoder3` is *not* the defect — the binding rule deliberately offers a level its own reward — so recording is the fix; withdrawing it from level 26's palette is the alternative if the controller prefers to protect that lesson, and is permitted by "may offer".

2. **`wide.ts:843` uses the operator the implementation warns against.** The section note says "The value published is `1 << sel`", while `createDecoderDef`'s own comment (`wide.ts:914-917`) says "`2 ** sel` and not `1 << sel`: `<<` converts through int32, so at a 5-bit select bit 31 would come out negative". Same file, two notations, one of them the rejected one — write `2 ** sel` (or "bit `sel` high") in the section note.
3. **`wide.ts:868` rationale is not true of `number`.** "`2 ** 5 = 32` is the widest value a `number` carries exactly" — JavaScript integers are exact to 2^53; the real ceiling is the project's 32-bit port carrier (`MAX_WIDE_WIDTH = 32`, `wide.ts:89`; `fitsWidth` special-cases width ≥ 32, `src/core/signal.ts:16-19`). The conclusion (w = 5, out = 32 bits) is right; reword the sentence.
4. **`test/core/defs-wide.test.ts:265` trades away a direction the old literal list checked.** The expectation now comes from the module tuples, so "every wide def has a row in this file's contract tables" is no longer asserted: a future family member added to a tuple would pass this test with no tabulated pin/price contract here. Covered today (the decoders' contract is explicit in `registry.test.ts:501-556`), and the report states the trade, but a one-line assertion that each wide id appears in some contract table — or a note naming where each family's contract lives — keeps the file's own promise.
5. **`batch3.ts:481-482` tells the player to drop `decoder2` in, and no palette offers it.** The ruled wording and the deliberate palette decision are both recorded (`batch3.ts:450-460`, `ch2-batch3.test.ts:1350`), so this is only the player-visible seam: the brief names a part that cannot be selected in this chapter.
6. **`batch3.ts:497-500` puts a design fact in the SOURCED half.** Level 26's SOURCED clause says "the same generator as level 25 one width up (… `decoder3` is `createDecoderDef(3)`)". The generator is this replica's mechanism; keeping it in the SOURCED sentence blurs the split the batch is otherwise careful about. Move the `createDecoderDef(3)` clause to AUTHORED.
7. **`registry.test.ts:501` asserts names only for `decoder1`/`decoder3`.** `decoder2`'s pins, price and behaviour are covered by the generator loop (`registry.test.ts:559`) but its generated name (`2 位解码器` / `2-Bit Decoder`) is not asserted anywhere; one extra row in `ROWS` covers it.

### Part 2: Code Quality

- **Structure.** The decoder family sits between the operators and the storage family with a section note in the file's own idiom (`wide.ts:822-841`, mirroring `THE STORAGE FAMILY (task 4)`), and is registered the way `wide.ts` registers its other families: a generator (`createDecoderDef`), a literal width list (`DECODER_WIDTHS`), a literal id tuple (`DECODER_DEF_IDS`), and `DECODER_DEFS = DECODER_WIDTHS.map(createDecoderDef)` — the same generator + literal-tuple shape as `WIDE_DEF_IDS`/`createWideDefs` and `WIDE_STORAGE_DEF_IDS`/`WIDE_STORAGE_DEFS`, with the two lists pinned to each other by a test (`registry.test.ts:559-566`). Not being a `createWideDefs` product is correct and documented: that generator forces one width on every pin (`wide.ts:822-836`), and a decoder's pins must differ. Refusing out-of-range widths rather than clamping diverges from `clampWidth` (`wide.ts:100-103`); the justification (clamping would silently hand back a part with a different pin shape) is sound, so the divergence is deliberate rather than an inconsistency.
- **Should it have been a `params.width` knob?** No — I verified the premise independently: `src/core/net.ts:98-99` is `inst.params.width ?? pin.width`, and the file's own doc at `net.ts:88` says `params.width` covers every pin of that instance; `net.ts:305` additionally joins a driver to a sink by `Math.min(driverWidth, sinkWidth)`, which is also why level 25's 8-bit `maker` into a 2-bit level output is legal. Ruling 1 is right, and the follow-up's replacement of the brief text is the correct resolution.
- **Are the comments load-bearing or noise?** Load-bearing, and each claim I spot-checked against the code is either a measurement or flagged as arithmetic (`batch3.ts:567-571` and `:571-580` do label the level-27 alternative as arithmetic rather than a measurement). The cost of the volume is that a stale claim survives review — which is precisely what issue 1 is. The module header earns its length by carrying cross-level facts (palette rule, not-joined status, reward-def seam) that no single level comment can own.
- **Do the tests verify behaviour rather than restate data?** Mostly behaviour: decoder tables written out by hand and checked against `evaluate`; one-hotness and the "not `sel`" reading; the category assertion derived from independent tuples; opcode coverage and break-one-opcode variants; counterexample failure records recomputed from pure functions; palette walks in both directions with the storage family asserted unreachable. The one restatement is `hands out the parts the brief assigns to each level` (`ch2-batch3.test.ts:457`), which is legitimate pinning of the brief's unlock column, and the SOURCED/AUTHORED marker test (`:488`) is a string presence check — weak by nature, which is why the substantive check for it is reading the comments, as this review did.

### Assessment

**Task quality:** Needs fixes

**Reasoning:** The five levels, the decoder family and the corrected level-25 brief are in substance correct — one-hot decoders verified against the defs, 1/10/27 derived and cross-checked, targets asserted equal to their own references' measurements, counterexamples graded-and-wrong, opcode coverage measured rather than assumed, and no existing score moveable by the diff; the single defect is that `batch3.ts:57-58` states level 25 is the only level answered by a part it offers, when level 26's own reward `decoder3` does the same and the batch neither records nor measures it.

Two reviews approved the substance — targets asserted equal to measured metrics, counterexamples graded-and-wrong, non-vacuous fuzz, accurate SOURCED/AUTHORED blocks — and raised the items below. One of them corrects a ruling **I** got wrong, so read that one carefully.

## Fix 1 (Important) — a module note is false at the commit that made it false

`src/levels/content/ch2/batch2.ts`'s module note (around lines 45–57) says of `full_adder`: "NO DEF OF THAT ID IS REGISTERED", "`src/core/defs/index.ts` lists no `full_adder`", "the only mentions of one in the project are the design spec and this note", and it hands a later task two open decisions. The same claim is repeated in level 20's comment (around lines 325–330) and in `test/levels/ch2-batch2.test.ts` (around line 51).

Commit `523a7b9` — the head of that very range — **registered** the def (`src/core/defs/index.ts`, `gateCost: FULL_ADDER`). So the file's normative note now misdirects a later reader into work already done.

Rewrite all three as history plus the live facts: the def did not exist when the level was authored; it was registered in `523a7b9` at 9 NAND-equivalents per the shared `FULL_ADDER` basis; it is offered at level 20 only (see Fix 2). Keep whatever is genuinely still open.

## Fix 2 (Important) — reconcile `full_adder`'s post-reward availability, the code's way

I ruled that `full_adder` be offered at levels 20 **and** 21. The implementer offered it at 20 only, withholding it at 21, and argued the case. Its argument is better than my ruling, and the reviewer agreed with it independently:

- Level 21's source achievement is "仅用 5 个蓝色元件" (only 5 blue components), which this replica maps to a **measured gate threshold of 15**.
- A 9-gate `full_adder` drop-in scores three stars against that 15-gate target, which voids the five-component lesson the level exists to teach.
- My rationale for 20–21 was "level 22's lesson is the cascade" — which does not actually reach level 21.

**So the ruling is amended to: `full_adder` is offered at level 20 only.** Your job is to make the code, the comments, and this rationale agree, and to remove the dead-end:

- The part is currently handed out at level 20 and offered by **no later level**, which makes it dead content. Level 22 is the cascade that consumes full adders conceptually. Decide and implement **one** of:
  - **(a) Offer `full_adder` at level 22** as well, and re-measure level 22's `threeStar` from its reference if the presence of a cheap drop-in changes what the target separates. Note in the comment what the drop-in scores versus the reference, so the target's meaning is explicit.
  - **(b) Leave it at 20 only** and record plainly in level 20's comment that the part is a convenience offered for that level and re-offered in a later chapter, so a reader does not think it is an oversight.
  Choose (a) if it can be done without making level 22's own targets trivial; otherwise (b). **State which you chose and why** in the report. Do not leave the ruling, the comments and the data disagreeing.
- Level 21's comment (around lines 385–394) argues *against* my old ruling; rewrite it to state the settled position and the reason, so it reads as a decision rather than a contradiction.
- Also fix the clause the reviewer found false read literally (around lines 380–381): "the gate target is what denies three stars to a player who spends a sixth gate" is wrong, because six NAND-equivalents is ≤ 15 and passes. The real point is that the source's "5 components" is not 15 NAND-equivalents. Say it that way.

## Fix 3 (Important) — level 26 has the same unrecorded seam as level 25

`src/levels/content/ch2/batch3.ts`'s module header (around lines 57–58) claims "the one part a level in this batch both offers and is answered by is level 25's OWN reward, `decoder1`". That is false about its own batch: level 26's palette lists `decoder3` (its own reward), whose pins are exactly level 26's I/O, so one drop-in scores gate 27 / delay 1 / tick 0 against the level's gate-27 / delay-3 target — three stars, bypassing the "share the low decode" lesson.

Offering a level its own reward is the deliberate rule, so **recording is the fix**, not withdrawal:

- Correct the header sentence to name both cases.
- Add level 26 the same treatment level 25 already has: a comment paragraph stating that its own reward answers it in one drop-in, with the measured numbers, and a test that grades a `decoder3` instance against `ch2-26-3-bit-decoder` and compares its metrics with the level's `threeStar` (level 25's test at roughly `test/levels/ch2-batch3.test.ts:1353` is your model).
- If you conclude level 26's lesson is better protected by **withdrawing** `decoder3` from its palette, that is permitted ("may offer"), but say so explicitly and record the cost. Either way the batch must no longer contain an unrecorded trivialisation.

## Fix 4 (Minor) — level 22's palette comment over-claims

`src/levels/content/ch2/batch2.ts` around lines 34–43 and 472–475 states the palette rule as "everything unlocked whose pins attach, plus own rewards, minus any part that would answer the level", and says level 22 offers "everything else on the player's wide shelf". Level 22's palette also omits the seven byte operators unlocked at 18/19 (`and8 or8 nand8 nor8 xor8 xnor8 not8`), which are neither own rewards nor self-answering — so either the rule or the comment is wrong. Name the omission as a third documented category, or add them; do not leave the note describing a palette the code does not build.

## Fix 5 (Minors, quick text corrections in `src/core/defs/wide.ts`)

Two claims are wrong even though their conclusions are right:
- The decoder section note says the published value is `1 << sel`, while `createDecoderDef`'s own comment explains that `2 ** sel` is used precisely because `<<` converts through int32 and would go negative at bit 31. Use `2 ** sel` (or "bit `sel` high") in the section note too — do not leave one file recommending the notation its own code rejects.
- A rationale says "`2 ** 5 = 32` is the widest value a `number` carries exactly". JavaScript integers are exact to 2^53; the real ceiling is the project's 32-bit port carrier (`MAX_WIDE_WIDTH`). Reword while keeping the conclusion (width 5, 32-bit output).

## Fix 6 (Minor) — a SOURCED/AUTHORED blur

`src/levels/content/ch2/batch3.ts` around lines 497–500 puts a design fact in level 26's SOURCED clause: "the same generator as level 25 one width up (`decoder3` is `createDecoderDef(3)`)". The generator is this replica's mechanism, not the source's. Move that clause to the AUTHORED half. The source genuinely does list a `2-Bit Decoder | 2-to-4 解码器` (I verified it against the compendium at §8.1), so the sourcing of `decoder2`'s existence may stay.

## Not in scope

- `test/levels/level-buildability.test.ts` not yet walking batch 2 — the assembly task is editing that file right now. Leave it alone.
- `src/levels/checks.ts`'s `generateRows` typing, and hoisting the duplicated `vacuityProblems` helper into `test/fixtures/`. Both are recorded as deferred; a later task owns them.
- Do not restate or re-measure any target that is not affected by Fix 2. Every `threeStar` currently equals its reference's measured metrics and must still afterwards.

## Files in scope

`src/levels/content/ch2/batch2.ts`, `src/levels/content/ch2/batch3.ts`,
`test/levels/ch2-batch2.test.ts`, `test/levels/ch2-batch3.test.ts`, `src/core/defs/wide.ts`
(text corrections only — do not change any def's behaviour, pins, `cost` or `gateCost`).
Nothing else. Another agent is writing `test/levels/level-buildability.test.ts`,
`test/levels/unlock-chain.test.ts`, `test/fixtures/ch2-references.ts`, `src/levels/content/index.ts`
and `src/levels/content/ch2/index.ts` — do not touch those.

## Testing

- Every `threeStar` must still equal its reference's measured metrics after your changes, and every
  counterexample must still fail. If Fix 2(a) changes level 22's palette, re-measure its target.
- Add the level-26 measurement test from Fix 3.
- Full suite green; `tsc --noEmit`; `pnpm build`.

Commands (from the worktree; bare `pnpm` on PATH is a broken wrapper):
- focused: `node "C:\Users\ME\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\node\bin\node.exe" "C:\Users\ME\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\pnpm\bin\pnpm.mjs" test <file>`
- full: `... pnpm.mjs test`   - typecheck: `... pnpm.mjs exec tsc --noEmit`   - build: `... pnpm.mjs build`

Redirect full-suite, tsc and build output to log files beside your report and reference them.

## Your Job

1. Apply Fixes 1–6.
2. Append a report to
   `D:\Documents\turing-complete\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase1\task-11-report.md`
   (a new heading is fine) with: each fix, your Fix 2 choice and why, the level-26 measurement, the
   covering tests, and the exact commands and output.
3. Commit. **Do not commit** `.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase1/progress.md`
   (the controller's ledger) — leave it modified.
4. Reply with ONLY: **Status** (DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT), commit short SHA
   + subject, one-line test summary, concerns, report path.

## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

Do all of this yourself. Never spawn a subagent or a reviewer.

## If You're in Over Your Head

`BLOCKED` is fine. If Fix 2(a) cannot be done without trivialising level 22's targets, take (b) and
say so — that is a legitimate answer, not a failure. If you disagree with the amendment to my ruling,
say so explicitly in the report rather than complying silently; I would rather hear the argument."}

and phase-end verification including a smoke test that a chapter-2 level actually opens).
  This task merges the plan's Task 7 (assembly) and Task 12 (verification) per the batching ruling.

## Review results for the content batches

Task 8+9 review (levels 13–22, range e8ba629..523a7b9): **Needs fixes** — no behavioural or
  level-data defect. Verified rather than accepted: all ten `SOURCED`/`AUTHORED` comments accurate,
  all ten `threeStar` asserted **equal** to their references' measured metrics, all ten counterexamples
  graded-and-wrong, fuzz non-vacuous (256 captured vectors, >100 distinct, recomputed first-disagreement
  round), `full_adder`'s 8-row table correct and its `gateCost` genuinely reusing the shared constant,
  and the palette change a chapter-1 no-op **proved by construction** (no chapter-1 level lists its own
  reward, so the added names are filtered back out by `allowedComponents`).
  One process failure of mine: the review package for that range was never written (the reviewer had to
  materialize the diff itself). My `review-package` call for that range was superseded when I
  re-generated a corrected range for a different review and did not go back. Recorded so the mistake is
  visible; it cost the reviewer a step, not the correctness of the review.

Ruling: **amend my own ruling 4 from "`full_adder` is offered at levels 20–21" to "at level 20 only"**
(the code already did the latter). The implementer withheld it at level 21 and argued the case; the
reviewer agreed independently. My rationale was "level 22's lesson is the cascade", which does not
reach level 21 — and level 21's lesson is the source's "仅用 5 个蓝色元件", mapped to a **measured
15-gate threshold**, against which a 9-gate `full_adder` drop-in scores three stars and voids the
lesson the level exists to teach. — Cost if wrong: the player cannot use the part they just earned in
the next level, which is exactly the "reward the player never gets to use" smell; the fix round is
required to decide and record where the reward is actually used (re-offered at level 22, or recorded as
a convenience for level 20 and re-offered in a later chapter) so it does not stay dead content.

Task 10 review (levels 23–27, decoders): **Needs fixes** — one Important item, and it is the same
  species as one this phase has already fixed twice. Verified: decoders are genuinely one-hot (the
  "not `sel`" reading is actively hunted by a test rather than assumed away), `gateCost` 1/10/27 is
  arithmetically derived and cross-checks both level targets, the category assertion is **not** a
  tautology (it derives from literal registration tuples that are independent of the defs'
  `category` fields), level 27's eight opcodes are genuinely exercised, and no existing score can move
  because no existing def literal was edited.
  The finding: `batch3.ts`'s header claims level 25 is the **only** level answered by a part it offers,
  but level 26's own reward `decoder3` has exactly level 26's I/O shape and one drop-in scores three
  stars — unrecorded and unmeasured, unlike level 25's own case which is both. Same class as `add8` at
  22 and `neg8` at 24: a part that answers its own level.

Task 10: source fact **verified by me** rather than accepted — the compendium's §8.1 component catalog
  really does list `2-Bit Decoder | 2-to-4 解码器`, so `decoder2`'s existence is sourced and the
  SOURCED wording for it is correct. The reviewer flagged this as unverifiable from the diff and asked
  me to confirm; confirmed against the source file.

content.text:
We need to add `ram8` to the spec's component list since it's used in level 37, correct the documentation error in the spec that mislabels it as `ram8` when it should be `switch` or `switch8`, and clarify the spec text around line 116 where the original note about switches at level 32 was recorded.The real issue is that level 22 uses switches as data selectors for its 8-bit adder implementation, but the spec's teaching note says switches shouldn't appear until level 32. Since moves 22 and 32 both use them, the cleanest fix is to update the spec to reflect that switches unlock at level 22 where they're actually needed, and then reorder the chapter-2 levels so the Bit Switch level becomes 22 instead of 32. The key insight is that level numbering follows the source's table structure rather than component unlock order—so moving `switch` to level 22 means deviating from the source's own progression, which I've already done with other components like `full_adder` and `mem1`. I've already made these reordering decisions and documented them, so this is just another explicit trade-off to record.

I'm accepting this divergence as a consequence of the design and will document it clearly: level 22 gets `switch`/`switch8`, level 32's Bit Switch level then re-teaches the same component with different framing, and I'll update the spec notes accordingly while recording the source-order deviation. Now I need to verify that level 32 doesn't need to reward `switch` again—once it's unlocked earlier, the level can still list it without creating a duplicate reward.

On the chapter-1 test assertion changes: those tests were checking that chapter 2 wasn't joined yet, which is now false by construction. Removing them is correct and necessary.

There's a coordination issue to flag: the assembly and content-fix tasks ran in parallel and the assembly agent briefly swept up another agent's work, though it self-corrected with an amend. I need to be careful about parallel writers in the same worktree going forward, and verify the final tree once my own edits are done.

Now I'm looking at Fix 2(a) regarding level 22—it offers full_adder but the drop-in solution scores 72/8 at 3 stars versus the reference at 120/17. I need to check whether the level's target still separates these solutions.

The drop-in actually scores better on both gate count and delay than the reference, so the reference isn't optimal anymore. But the threeStar target is supposed to be the reference's own measurement, which creates a contradiction. Either I need to update the reference to the better solution and re-measure the target, or reconsider the whole approach.

I'm weighing two options: (b) withdraw full_adder at level 22 so the cascade stays optimal, though that makes the level's rewards dead content; or (c) keep full_adder available and set the reference to the eight-full_adder drop-in instead, which gives a lower target and preserves the "measure from the best reference" principle.

The tension is that (c) wouldn't actually enforce the intended 8-bit adder design—it'd just be eight instances in a row. But looking at level 22's purpose, it's teaching that 8-bit addition comes from cascading 1-bit adders, so either approach genuinely demonstrates that lesson. The cheap drop-in isn't a loophole; it's the lesson itself made concrete.

So (c) makes sense and honors the design boundary—the part doesn't work at level 21 because that level's lesson is the source's five-component constraint, not the cascade principle. I need to verify that level 22's new reference passes and isn't circular, then update the target.

Now I'm weighing whether choosing the better reference is worth the rework or if option (b) is simpler and just as defensible. Option (b) keeps the data unchanged, but it violates the principle that a part should be usable in the chapter. Option (c) requires updating the reference and targets but gives the player the best tool to actually construct the 8-bit adder. Let me go with (c)—it's the stronger design choice.

I also need to update the spec notes at §3.3. Since the spec is the binding authority, leaving it outdated would create the same inconsistency I've been avoiding. Now I'll update the ledger with these rulings and move into the verification and final review phase.
Both landed. The content fix took option (a) and disclosed that level 22's target no longer separates the drop-in — which means the *reference* is no longer optimal. Ruling on the five items:

{"description": "Close spec and unlock-chain consistency", "prompt": "You are closing two consistency gaps at the end of a phase. Work from `D:\Documents\turing-complete\.worktrees\phase1` (git worktree, branch `phase1`). Do all work there.

## Context

A from-scratch replica of the puzzle game *Turing Complete*. Chapter 2 (26 levels, indices 13–38) is
assembled, the full suite is green at 915 tests, and the browser suite proves chapter 2 is playable.
The design spec is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-25-turing-complete-replica-design.md`.

Two small inaccuracies remain, both about the spec's §3.3 component table — the document that is
supposed to be this project's authority. Both are mine to fix and I have ruled on them.

## Fix 1 — `mem1` is in the wrong row of §3.3's table

§3.3's table has one row per chapter listing the components that chapter unlocks. `mem1` is currently
named in the **chapter-2** row, but it is unlocked by **chapter-1 level 12** (`ch1-12-binary-racer`
rewards it — that reward was added earlier in this phase precisely to make chapter 2's latch level
buildable, because `mem1` had been rewarded by no level at all).

Move `mem1` to the **chapter-1** row, next to `delay_line`, and remove it from the chapter-2 row.
Keep the chapter-2 row otherwise as it is (it should still name `ram8`, which was just added).

While you are there, **verify the whole table against the data rather than trusting this prompt**:
every component named in a row should be unlocked by a level in that chapter, and every component
unlocked by a level should appear in that chapter's row. Report any other mismatch you find rather
than silently fixing it — one of them may be a deliberate design note rather than an error.

## Fix 2 — `test/levels/unlock-chain.test.ts` pins the spec's old state

That test hard-copies the chapter-2 component names (a 33-name list) and asserts that the one chapter-2
reward outside it is `['ram8']`. Since `ram8` has now been **added** to the spec, the assertion still
passes while pinning the pre-ruling state, and its header and comments still describe the `ram8` and
`switch`-level disagreements as live.

`ram8` was only ever an example of a general problem: **the test's expectation is a hand-maintained copy
of the thing it is checking**, so it cannot detect that the spec changed. This is the third time in this
phase that a hard-coded list tracking generated/derived data has hidden a change.

Rewrite it so its expectation comes from the spec itself. The design spec is markdown, and this project's
test files already read files from disk (look for the `node:fs` + `@ts-expect-error` pattern used
elsewhere in the level tests, since there is no `@types/node`). Two acceptable forms — pick one and say
which and why:

- **(a)** Parse §3.3's chapter-2 row out of the spec markdown and assert the level data's rewards match it.
- **(b)** Derive the expected set from the level data and assert the spec's row **contains** it (which
  catches a component the spec forgot, though not one the spec adds that no level uses).

Then: remove the now-obsolete `extra === ['ram8']` assertion (or make it assert `[]` if your chosen form
keeps an `extra` notion), and rewrite the header paragraph, the `ram8` comment and the `switch` test's
title so they describe the **settled** state, not two live disagreements. The `switch` case is settled:
`switch`/`switch8` arrive at level 22 in this replica, the spec now says so, and the source's own level 32
is a re-teach here. Do not delete the `switch` test — it should still assert exactly one unlock each, and
its comments should say that the level number deliberately differs from the source's.

**Do not weaken rule 2.** It must still fail if a component is rewarded by zero levels or by two.

## Files in scope

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-25-turing-complete-replica-design.md`,
`test/levels/unlock-chain.test.ts`.

Nothing else. **Commit only these two files** — never `git add -A`; a concurrent agent's in-flight work
being swept into a commit already cost this phase real time once.

## Testing

- Full suite green (expect 915 tests; adjust the count only if your rewrite legitimately changes it, and
  say so).
- **Prove the test can still fail.** Temporarily remove a component from the spec's chapter-2 row (or
  from a level's rewards) and confirm the test goes red, then restore it. Report the mutation and its
  output — a rewritten assertion that cannot fail is worse than the hard-coded one it replaced.
- `tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm build`.

Commands (from the worktree; bare `pnpm` on PATH is a broken wrapper):
- focused: `node "C:\Users\ME\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\node\bin\node.exe" "C:\Users\ME\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\pnpm\bin\pnpm.mjs" test <file>`
- full: `... pnpm.mjs test`   - typecheck: `... pnpm.mjs exec tsc --noEmit`   - build: `... pnpm.mjs build`

Redirect full-suite, tsc and build output to log files beside your report and reference them.

## Your Job

1. Apply both fixes.
2. Append a report to
   `D:\Documents\turing-complete\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase1\task-12-report.md`
   under a new heading: the spec table check (including any mismatch you found and did not fix), your
   chosen form for the unlock-chain rewrite and why, the mutation proof, the covering tests, and the
   exact commands and output.
3. Commit. **Do not commit** `.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase1/progress.md`
   (the controller's ledger) — leave it modified.
4. Reply with ONLY: **Status** (DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT), commit short SHA
   + subject, one-line test summary, concerns, report path.

## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

Do this yourself. Never spawn a subagent or a reviewer.

## If You're in Over Your Head

`BLOCKED` is fine. If parsing the spec markdown turns out to be brittle in a way that would make the test
fail for formatting reasons rather than data reasons, **take form (b)** and say so — a test that breaks
when someone reflows a table is not worth having."}

Repository: `D:\Documents\turing-complete\.worktrees\phase1` (git worktree, branch `phase1`, 31 commits). Read-only: do not mutate the working tree, index, HEAD, or branch state.

## What this branch is

A from-scratch replica of the puzzle game *Turing Complete* — a NAND-to-CPU logic game — built from a user-supplied research compendium. **Phase 0** (already merged to `master`) shipped the simulation kernel, canvas board, level framework, scoring, save system, and chapter 1 (12 levels). **This branch is Phase 1**: the multi-bit (8-bit) component system plus chapter 2 (26 levels, indices 13–38), for **38 levels total**.

The design spec is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-25-turing-complete-replica-design.md` — read §3.3 (component model and unlock order), §5.2–§5.4 (checker kinds, scoring, stars) and §12 (phase acceptance criteria). The plan is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase1.md`. Phase 1's acceptance criterion from the spec is: **"26 关回归通过；锁存器/振荡器/计数器测试通过"** — all 26 levels pass regression, and latch/oscillator/counter tests pass.

## Global constraints that bind the whole branch

- **Zero runtime dependencies.** `dependencies` must be empty; everything is in `devDependencies`, versions pinned.
- Layering is one-way: `ui → app → levels → core`, `persist → app`. `core/` may not import upward.
- **Signals are `0`/`1`; a multi-bit port is a run of consecutive 1-bit slots, never packed.** The signal table has a fixed capacity decided at compile time and never reallocates.
- **Every component contributes exactly 1 unit of delay; storage contributes 0** (`sequential: true` breaks the combinational path both ways). `SETTLE_LIMIT = 512`. The settle loop is a parallel/Jacobi sweep so a two-inverter ring is detectable.
- **The storage contract**: `evaluate` publishes held state and may read **at most** one input that only selects among bytes already in `state`; `clockEdge` samples inputs into state and never writes outputs.
- **Scoring**: `score = gate + delay*4 + tick*8`; **`gate` is NAND-equivalents and `cost` is the per-node delay unit** — different quantities that coincide only for `nand`/`not`. Stars are 0/1/3 only; a metric **equal** to its target counts as met.
- **A level is pure data**; adding levels must not require engine changes.
- **Source fidelity, the branch's most important discipline.** The compendium supplies **only** the level names, their order, and a one-line teaching concept — no truth tables, ports, widths, pass conditions, or rewards. Every level must carry a `SOURCED`/`AUTHORED` comment, and **no authored choice may be presented as sourced.** Level `brief`/`hint` prose must be original (the README claims the project contains none of the original game's text); level *names* are exempt.

## Verification already done (do not re-run; treat as established)

At commit `901dda4`: `pnpm test` → **23 files / 918 tests passed**; `pnpm build` clean; `pnpm smoke` → **5 passed**, including level 13 opening after chapter 1, a chapter-2 level built and graded end to end with a star written, and level 38 reachable. These were run independently by the controller in a clean shell, not only reported by implementers.

The per-task reviews already verified, per task: spec compliance, targets asserted equal to their references' measured metrics, counterexamples genuinely failing, non-vacuous fuzz checks, the storage contract per def, and chapter-1 palettes unchanged.

## What YOU must look for — the things per-task reviews could not see

1. **Cross-cutting coherence of chapter 2 as a curriculum.** Do the 26 levels form a learnable progression, and does every level's `allowedComponents` give the player what its own reference solution needs? The branch has a buildability test for this — check what it actually proves and whether it can be evaded.
2. **Whether the phase actually meets its acceptance criterion** (spec §12) rather than merely passing tests. In particular, are latch, oscillator and counter genuinely tested as behaviour?
3. **The three latent kernel defects this phase existed to fix**, and whether any path around them remains: a wide input read contiguously from a narrow driver; `inputBase` handing back a narrow driver's base for a wider pin; and pin widths resolved from the definition instead of per instance.
4. **Whether the gate/delay metric split is now coherent end to end** — `cost` for delay, `gateCost` for gates — or whether another surface still conflates them.
5. **Any place where the branch's own discipline was broken**: an authored value presented as sourced, a test that asserts nothing, a hand-maintained list tracking generated data (this happened three times in the phase), a doc that promises enforcement the code does not perform, or a comment that is false at its own commit.
6. **Real defects in the new code**, especially `src/core/net.ts` (the publish mechanism and read regions), `src/core/defs/wide.ts` (the 8-bit operator, storage and decoder families), and `src/levels/checks.ts` (the fuzz and custom checkers and the `runChecks` dispatch).

## Triage these deferred findings — which must be fixed before merge?

The phase ledger parked these as non-blocking. Read the ledger for detail:
`.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase1/progress.md` (search for `minor (deferred)`).

- `levels/checks.ts:1046` casts `'(none)' as CheckFailure['check']` — a value outside the kind union, with no reader today.
- The element guard's ordering test would still pass if the guard moved after `createSim`, so it pins less than its name claims.
- A throwing `kind` accessor, and an outcome whose getters are hostile only on a **second** read, still escape `runChecks`.
- The `custom`-checker tick count is trusted, so a checker could understate ticks and inflate a star rating (no checker ships yet).
- `src/levels/grader.ts`: a comment says the `?? cost` fallback is for defs "zero on both", but a synthetic `cost: 1` def legitimately uses it.
- `toUint`'s `Uint8Array` branch is unexercised (it is the carrier for a later phase's 16/32-bit defs).
- `makeOp` has a negative intermediate at width 32 (the returned value is correct).
- `wide.ts`'s `splitter`/`maker` cannot be instantiated at a non-8 pin count; per-instance counts would need a def-level hook in `net.ts`.
- The UI (`src/ui/truthTable.ts`) does not render the new `detail`/`round` fields, so a fuzz or malformed-custom failure shows the player a row of zeros.
- `checks.ts` has grown to ~1081 lines hosting four responsibilities; the fuzz block is the obvious extraction.
- `generateRows` is typed against `LevelSpec` while reading only `io`, so level data passes it a fake spec object.
- The chapter-1 test files' frozen metrics are not compared against their targets (a chapter-1 score could fall while staying inside its target, invisibly).
- `decoder2` is registered and named in the spec row but unlocked by no level — a deliberate divergence, pinned from both sides.

**Base:** `405b4978ad030d7129dc7fa7a0ecffd38b82d510` (the commit `master` is at; the branch point)
**Head:** `901dda4fc634e59cfdb1ed88e531155761b62e18`
**Diff file:** `D:\Documents\turing-complete\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase1\review-405b497..901dda4.diff`

## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

Do all of this yourself. Never spawn a subagent, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion.

Implementer reports and the ledger are claims, not evidence. The ledger is written by the controller (me) and is therefore also self-assessment. Verify against the code.

## Output Format

### Phase Acceptance
Does the branch meet spec §12's Phase 1 criterion? State the evidence you checked, not the test count.

### Spec Compliance
- ✅ / ❌ with file:line
- ⚠️ Cannot verify

### Deferred-Finding Triage
For each parked finding above: **Must fix before merge** | **Fix later** | **Stand as-is**, with one line of reasoning. Be willing to say most of them stand.

### Issues
#### Critical (Must Fix)
#### Important (Should Fix)
#### Minor (Nice to Have)

For each: file:line, what's wrong, why it matters, how to fix if not obvious.

### Strengths
Specific, and only where earned.

### Assessment
**Merge readiness:** [Ready to merge | Needs fixes first]
**Reasoning:** [2-3 sentences.]

## Calibration

Not everything is Critical. Important means the branch cannot be trusted until fixed. "Coverage could be broader" is Minor. Do not manufacture findings to look thorough — if the branch is sound, saying so is the correct answer, and the controller would rather merge on an honest clean verdict than chase invented work. Equally, do not let the branch's own extensive commentary substitute for verification: check what the code does, not what its comments say it does.

Your final message is the report itself: begin directly with the phase-acceptance verdict. Every line is a verdict, a finding with file:line, or a check you ran — no preamble, no process narration, no closing summary."}

- The kernel fixes are minimal, at the right layer, and each is pinned by a test that would fail on the pre-fix behaviour (slot-layout reproduction; `inputBase`+`read` coherence after `settle`; per-instance width through `params.width` on both level IO and a def's own pin).

- The unlock/palette invariants are machine checks over the shipped set (buildability walk using the app's own function; §3.3 parsed from the spec; exactly-one-unlocker rule with one *named and separately tested* exception; a reference circuit for every shipped id).

### Assessment
**Merge readiness:** Ready to merge.
**Reasoning:** The phase meets §12's criterion on evidence rather than on test counts — all 26 levels' references grade to a pass against targets asserted equal to their own measurements, and latch/oscillator/counter are exercised as behaviour from both sides (settles vs throws, periodicity vs ungated/stuck, wrap vs no-reset). That review returned **Ready to merge** with 0 Critical and 0 Important findings plus seven Minors; the fixes below were applied after it. Your job is to verdict each fix and inspect the fix diff for new breakage — nothing else. This is the last gate before the branch merges.

Repository: `D:\Documents\turing-complete\.worktrees\phase1` (git worktree, branch `phase1`). Read-only: do not mutate the working tree, index, HEAD, or branch state.

## Context

A from-scratch replica of the puzzle game *Turing Complete*. The branch is Phase 1: the multi-bit (8-bit) component system plus chapter 2 (26 levels, indices 13–38), 38 levels total. Established at `901dda4`: 23 test files, 918 tests, clean build, and a browser smoke suite proving level 13 opens, a chapter-2 level builds and grades end to end, and level 38 is reachable. The whole-branch review verified phase acceptance against spec §12.

## The fixes under verification

**From the final review's Minor list:**

1. **`maskOf(31)` returned a negative mask**, and two operators returned it as a port value: `divideOp`'s divide-by-zero and `shiftRightArithmeticOp`'s sign fill, in `src/core/defs/wide.ts`. Required: `w >= 32 ? 0xffff_ffff : 2 ** w - 1`, with a test at width 31 and 32. The implementer reported that the instruction's stated line content did not match the committed blob — the blob read `(1 << w) - 1` for the narrow arm — and that it proved the bug by executing the real `evaluate` path before editing.
2. **The failure panel fabricated a test vector.** `src/ui/truthTable.ts` rendered a row of `0`s when a failure's `inputs`/`expected`/`actual` maps were all empty, which is reachable via the `unstable` reason — i.e. level 28 and level 30, the levels whose lesson is that an ungated loop never settles. Required: show the reason/detail instead, with a test.
3. **Level 27's SOURCED block claimed completeness it lacked**, omitting the source's `Symmetric ALU` achievement (only 8-bit-family parts). Required: delete the completeness claim and record the achievement as sourced-but-ungraded, like levels 21/22/38 do. No change to checks, palette, reference or targets.
4. **Chapter 1 had no exact-target assertion** (only `stars === 3`), so a loosened chapter-1 target was invisible. Required: add the same `threeStar === measured metrics` equality the 26 chapter-2 levels have. All 12 were expected to already agree.
5. **Seven stale/false statements**, each false at its own commit: `batch4.ts`'s "NOT JOINED YET"; `registry.test.ts`'s "written-but-unjoined" comment and now-dead union; the plan's `mem1`-at-level-8 and `decoder1`/`decoder2`-via-`params.width` claims; `wide.ts`'s claim that no def leans on the `?? cost` fallback; the spec's justification for level 22's `switch` unlock; a test quoting a "48-gate circuit" where the comment says 54; and spec §5.4's delay-unit and "achievements直接成为门槛" sentences.

**Discovered during the wave and fixed after it:**

6. **`src/core/signal.ts`'s `fitsWidth` used `v < 1 << width`**, so `1 << 31` is negative and `assertWidth(v, 31)` rejected *every* value including 0. Fixed to `v < 2 ** width` with a boundary sweep over every width 1..32. The implementer kept the `width >= 32` fast path, justifying it because `MAX_PARAM_WIDTH` reaches 4096 and `setPort`'s number branch (`(v >>> i) & 1`) carries at most 32 bits.
7. **That fast path omitted `v >= 0`**, so `setPort(base, 32, -1)` was accepted and silently read back as `0xffff_ffff`. Fixed to `v >= 0 && v <= 0xffff_ffff`, with the fast path kept and the justification re-verified by reading `setPort`.
8. **A comment in `wide.ts` became false** once `signal.ts` was fixed (it still said width 31 could not be staged and that the repair was scope-blocked). Rewritten.

**Ratified as deferred — must NOT have been changed:** `src/core/fields.ts`'s dormant `insertField`/`extractField` width-31 pair (broken at 31, no `src/` caller); the level layer's absent pin-width cap (input-pin masks are unreachable because ≥31-bit input pins imply ≥2³¹ enumerated rows; a hand-authored wide *output* pin would get mask −1 or 1); the `'(none)'` cast; the element-guard ordering test; the hostile-getter escape; `custom` tick trust; the `grader.ts` `?? cost` wording; the unexercised `toUint` byte branch; `makeOp`'s negative intermediate; the `splitter`/`maker` pin-count limitation; `checks.ts`'s size; `generateRows`'s parameter type; `enumerateInputs`'s missing cap; the empty-`spec.checks` guard; and `decoder2` having no unlocker.

## What the Implementers Claim

The fix reports are appended to one file:
`D:\Documents\turing-complete\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase1\task-12-report.md`
Look for the sections covering the final-review wave and the width-guard tasks. Their evidence logs are in the same directory (`logs-*.log`, `task-12d-*.log`, `task-12e-*.log`). Read the ones you need.

## Diff Under Review

**Base:** `901dda4fc634e59cfdb1ed88e531155761b62e18` (the commit the whole-branch review saw)
**Head:** `5bce87a`
**Diff file:** `D:\Documents\turing-complete\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase1\review-901dda4..5bce87a.diff`

The range holds four commits: one controller ledger/doc commit (`cf152b4`, ignore its `progress.md` change), the seven-item fix wave (`99a3dcd`), the width-31 guard fix (`c830f50`), and the fast-path sign fix (`5bce87a`).

Read the diff file once — commit list, stat summary, full diff with context. Do not re-run git commands. You may read a specific file directly when you need context the diff truncates, and say so.

## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

Do all of this yourself. Never spawn a subagent, and never spawn another reviewer.

## Scope

Your scope is the eight fixes above and the fix diff. Verdict each. Inspect the fix diff for **new problems the fixes introduced** — that is the main risk here, because the wave touched the signal guard every value flows through and the panel the player reads. Do not re-review the branch as a whole; the whole-branch review already did that and returned Ready to merge.

## Tests

The implementers ran the tests with mutation proofs. Treat the reports as unverified claims: confirm they name the covering tests and show output, and verify the claims against the diff. Do not re-run the suite. Run a focused test only if reading the code raises a specific doubt no existing run answers.

## Verify these specifically, from the code rather than the reports

1. **Fix 6/7 are the highest-risk changes in the wave.** `fitsWidth` now bounds `v >= 0 && v <= 0xffff_ffff` on the fast path and `v >= 0 && v < 2 ** width` on the narrow arm. Confirm: (a) no previously-accepted value is now rejected, (b) no previously-rejected value is now accepted, for widths 1..32 and for the reachable-above-32 case, and (c) the fast path is genuinely still needed — verify the implementer's claim that `setPort`'s number branch carries at most 32 bits while widths to 4096 are reachable.
2. **Fix 1's `maskOf`.** Is `2 ** w - 1` correct and non-negative for every admitted `w`, and are the two port-returning operators (`divideOp` divide-by-zero, `shiftRightArithmeticOp` sign fill) now correct at 31 and 32? Check that `createWideDefs(31)` and `createWideDefs(32)` produce working defs.
3. **Fix 2's panel.** Does a failure with empty maps now show something truthful rather than a row of zeros, and does it still render normally when the maps are populated? The panel is player-facing: check that the change cannot throw on an unexpected failure shape.
4. **Fix 4's chapter-1 equality.** Confirm it is not vacuous — that loosening a chapter-1 target would actually fail it — and that no chapter-1 number was changed to make it pass.
5. **Fix 5's `registry.test.ts` item** was reported as a real defect rather than stale prose: the old union walked levels 13–27 three times over because `LEVELS` already contained every shipped level. Verify the union is now correct and minimal, and that the guards it feeds (the reward/palette walks and their non-vacuity anchors) are unchanged in strength.
6. **The ratified-deferred list**: confirm none of it was changed. In particular `src/core/fields.ts` must be untouched.

## Output Format

Your final message is the report itself: begin directly with the first fix's verdict. Every line is a verdict, a finding with file:line, or a check you ran — no preamble, no process narration.

### Fix Verdicts
For each of the eight fixes, in order:
- **[fix one-liner]** — ADDRESSED | NOT ADDRESSED, with file:line evidence. "Attempted" is not addressed: the defect must no longer exist.

### New Breakage in the Fix Diff
Anything the fixes broke or introduced, with severity (Critical/Important/Minor) and file:line. "None" if clean. Be specific about whether any change alters an accepted value, a grade, a score, or a level's solvability — those are the only categories that block the merge.

### Out-of-Scope Observations
Issues entirely outside the fix diff. Non-blocking. "None" if none.

### Verdict
**Fix wave:** [All fixes addressed, no new Critical/Important breakage | Findings remain open] — list any open ones, and state plainly whether the branch is still ready to merge."}

{"file_path": ".worktrees/phase1/.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase1/progress.md", "new_string": "final-review phase. That is strictly cheaper than a lost commit.

## Final review and the closing wave

Final whole-branch review (31 commits, `405b497..901dda4`): **Ready to merge. 0 Critical, 0 Important,
7 Minor.** Phase acceptance MET on evidence rather than test counts — the reviewer checked the 26
chapter-2 level names and their one-line concepts directly against the source compendium, confirmed
every level has a reference that grades to a pass with `threeStar` asserted **equal** to its own
measured metrics, and confirmed the spec §12 criterion (latch/oscillator/counter) is tested as
behaviour from both sides: the latch holds a byte across an input flip and reverts to a wire without
storage; the oscillator's 16-tick period is measured out of the check data with an ungated twin
failing at exactly tick 16 and a stuck source at tick 1; the counter walks 256 enabled edges, the
wrap, reset-over-enable and a same-tick hold. It also confirmed the three latent kernel defects are
closed with no remaining call path around them.

The review **re-derived two of my numbers rather than trusting them** and found one wrong prediction of
mine: it recomputed level 27's `668 = 497 + 171` gate arithmetic by hand (the mux is 3 NANDs because
`~s` is shared per stage) and re-derived the 8-deep delay path, and it reproduced `maskOf(31)` in node
to confirm a bug I had described from arithmetic alone.

Ruling: the fix wave is applied as **one** dispatch, not one per finding, and is followed by exactly
one scoped re-review. This is the skill's prescription for final-review findings and it is also what the
evidence supports: seven of the nine items were comment-only, one was a user-visible UI defect, and one
was a latent arithmetic bug in a generator no shipped part exercises. — Cost if wrong: a fix that
belonged to a different owner is bundled with the rest; the re-review verdicts each fix individually.

Ruling: `fitsWidth`'s width-32 fast path **keeps** its `0xffff_ffff` bound *and* gains the `v >= 0`
half. I initially left the negative case alone as beyond the assigned bug, the implementer reported it
as the only hole left in that guard, and the re-review verified the fast path is load-bearing: widths
above 32 are reachable (`MAX_PARAM_WIDTH = 4096`) while `setPort`'s number writer is
`(v >>> i) & 1`, i.e. ToUint32, so the bound is what prevents admitting a value the writer would
truncate. The re-review corrected the implementer's stated reason for that (for `i >= 32` the writer
re-reads bit `i - 32` rather than zero-filling) while confirming the conclusion. — Cost if wrong:
`setPort(base, 32, -1)` is now rejected rather than silently reinterpreted as `0xffff_ffff`. No shipped
path stages a negative, so nothing that worked stops working.

Ruling: `src/core/fields.ts`'s dormant `insertField`/`extractField` width-31 pair stays **unfixed**.
`insertField(value, offset, 31, field)` throws for every field including 0, because it compares the
field against the negative mask arithmetically, while `extractField` is only accidentally right at 31
and returns a signed result at 32. **Neither has any caller in `src/`** — only tests at widths
2/6/8/24/32 — so the pair is unreachable in the shipped game and fixing it would be speculative work on
a module no code path uses. Recorded in `wide.ts`'s own comment so it is not lost, and carried to
Phase 5 where `fields.ts` is the natural tool for wide ports. — Cost if wrong: a latent trap for
whoever first wires `fields.ts` up; the mitigation is that the trap is now named in the source.

`src/levels/content/ch2/batch4.ts` around lines 116–118 contains a sentence added by the fix wave saying, in effect, that nothing imports a batch file directly except that batch's own test.

That is false. Verify it yourself and then correct it:
- `test/levels/ch2-batch2.test.ts`, `ch2-batch3.test.ts` and `ch2-batch4.test.ts` each import **earlier** batches.

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-25-turing-complete-replica-design.md` around line 473 has a clause added by the fix wave saying that level 28's reference uses `switch` "因为 switch 只算一个延迟单位而 AND 单元算两个" — i.e. because `switch` costs one delay unit where an AND costs two.

`src/levels/content/ch2/batch4.ts`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-25-turing-complete-replica-design.md`. Nothing else.

   `D:\Documents\turing-complete\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-25-turing-complete-phase1\task-12-report.md`
   under a new heading: what the false sentences said, what they now say, whether `switch` earns its

Do this yourself. Never spawn a subagent or a reviewer.

`BLOCKED` is fine. If you cannot determine why level 28's reference contains `switch`, report that and
fix only the sentence that is demonstrably false — do not write a new justification you cannot support
from the code."}

<skill_instructions>
# Finishing a Development Branch

## Overview

**Core principle:** Verify tests → Detect environment → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."

## Step 1: Verify Tests

Run the project's full test suite (`npm test` / `cargo test` / `pytest` / `go test ./...`).

**If tests fail**, report the failures and stop — the menu comes after a green suite:

```
Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

[Show failures]
```

**If tests pass:** continue to Step 2.

## Step 2: Detect Environment

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
# Capture now, while still inside the workspace — Step 5 changes directory
# before cleanup (Step 6) needs this value
WORKTREE_PATH=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
```

This determines which menu to show and how cleanup works:

| State | Menu | Cleanup |
|-------|------|---------|
| `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (normal repo) | Standard 3 options | No worktree to clean up |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, named branch | Standard 3 options | Provenance-based (see Step 6) |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, detached HEAD | Reduced 2 options (no merge) | Externally managed — leave in place |

## Step 3: Determine Base Branch

The base branch is whatever this work forked from — usually named in the
plan, the conversation, or the branch's upstream. If it is not already
known, ask: "This branch split from <your best guess> - is that correct?"
Confirm before merging: merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo.

## Step 4: Present Options

**Normal repo and named-branch worktree — present exactly these 3 options:**

```
Implementation complete. What would you like to do?

1. Merge back to <base-branch> locally
2. Push and create a Pull Request
3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

**Detached HEAD — present exactly these 2 options:**

```
Implementation complete. You're on a detached HEAD (externally managed workspace).

1. Push as new branch and create a Pull Request
2. Keep as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

Present the menu exactly as written — concise, with every option coming
from the list above. Discarding the work happens only in response to your
human partner explicitly asking for it (see "If your human partner asks to
discard the work" below). Wait for their answer; the integration decision
is theirs.

## Step 5: Execute Choice

### Option 1: Merge Locally

```bash
# Get main repo root for CWD safety
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"

# Merge first — verify success before removing anything
git checkout <base-branch>
git pull
git merge <feature-branch>

# Verify tests on merged result
<test command>
```

If tests fail on the merged result: stop, leave the worktree and branch in
place, and investigate — nothing has been pushed, so the merge is local
and recoverable.

Once the merged result is green: clean up the worktree (Step 6), then
delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -d <feature-branch>
```

### Option 2: Push and Create PR

```bash
git push -u origin <feature-branch>
# From a detached HEAD, name the new branch on the remote:
# git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch>
```

Then create the pull/merge request against <base-branch> with the forge's
tooling — its CLI if one is available, or the creation URL most forges
print when you push — following the repo's PR template and conventions if
present, and report the URL to your human partner.

Keep the worktree — your human partner iterates on PR feedback there.

### Option 3: Keep As-Is

Report: "Keeping branch <name>. Worktree preserved at <path>."

### If your human partner asks to discard the work

This path exists only as a response to an explicit request to throw the
work away. Confirm first:

```
This will permanently delete:
- Branch <name>
- All commits: <commit-list>
- Worktree at <path>

Type 'discard' to confirm.
```

Wait for that exact confirmation. When it arrives:

```bash
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"
```

Then clean up the worktree (Step 6) and force-delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -D <feature-branch>
```

## Step 6: Cleanup Workspace

**Runs for Option 1 and confirmed discards.** Options 2 and 3 always
preserve the worktree. Both callers have already changed directory to the
main repo root — worktree removal must run from outside the worktree —
and use the `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_COMMON`/`WORKTREE_PATH` values captured in
Step 2, from before that directory change.

**If `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON`:** Normal repo, no worktree to clean up. Done.

**If `WORKTREE_PATH` is under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`:** Superpowers
created this worktree — we own cleanup:

```bash
git worktree remove "$WORKTREE_PATH"
git worktree prune  # Self-healing: clean up any stale registrations
```

**If removal is refused** (`contains modified or untracked files`): the
worktree holds files that exist nowhere else — uncommitted plans, notes,
or scratch work. Never `--force` on your own initiative. Show your human
partner what is at stake and ask:

```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE_PATH" status --porcelain -uall
```

```
Worktree removal refused — these files were never committed:

<file list>

1. Commit them to <branch> before cleanup
2. Move them into <main repo root>
3. Delete them (unrecoverable)

Which?
```

Carry out the choice, then remove the worktree.

**Otherwise:** The host environment owns this workspace — leave it in
place. If your platform provides a workspace-exit tool, use it.

## Quick Reference

| Option | Merge | Push | Keep Worktree | Cleanup Branch |
|--------|-------|------|---------------|----------------|
| 1. Merge locally | yes | - | - | yes |
| 2. Create PR | - | yes | yes | - |
| 3. Keep as-is | - | - | yes | - |
| Discard (explicit request only) | - | - | - | yes (force) |

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Tests passed earlier this session" | Run the suite on the tree you are about to integrate. A green run only proves the tree it ran on. |
| "They obviously want it merged" | Integration is your human partner's decision. Present the menu and wait. |
| "They seem done with this feature — I'll offer to discard it" | The menu is complete as written. Discard happens only when your human partner asks for it in so many words. |
| "'Yeah, get rid of it' counts as confirmation" | Only the typed word `discard` authorizes deletion. |
| "The PR is up, so the worktree is clutter now" | PR feedback gets fixed in that worktree. It stays until the work lands. |
| "This other worktree looks stale — I'll clean it too" | Clean up only worktrees under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`. Everything else belongs to the host. |
| "Removal refused — `--force` is just finishing the cleanup" | The refusal means files exist only in that worktree. `--force` destroys them permanently. Show your human partner and ask. |
| "The merged-result failure is probably flaky" | A failing merged result stops everything. Branch and worktree stay put while you investigate. |
| "The base branch is obviously main" | Confirm the fork point or ask. Merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo. |
| "The push was rejected — force-push will fix it" | A rejected push means the remote moved. Investigate; force-push only on your human partner's explicit request. |
